# Rango Feature Map (Internal)

Package: `@rangojs/router`

> **Internal implementation map.** This documents all capabilities including
> internal-only APIs. It is not a public API reference. For the public contract,
> see the actual export surfaces in `package.json`. Runtime conditions point to
> source entrypoints; type conditions point to emitted declarations under
> `dist/types`.

Related docs:

- [Execution model](./execution-model.md) — runtime contract, middleware scope, revalidation guarantees
- [Feature-to-file map](./feature-file-map.md) — source ownership for each feature
- [Semantic change checklist](./semantic-change-checklist.md) — PR checklist for contract changes

---

| `./ssr`                     | Advanced HTML rendering bridge: `createSSRHandler`, nonce/form-state/streamMode support. PPR shell (axis 2, opt-in): `createShellCaptureHandler` -> `captureShellHTML` (static `prerender` + abort -> prelude bytes + `postponed` state, sanity-gated) and `createShellResumeHandler` -> `resumeShellHTML` (resume fizz over a fresh `SsrRoot` for just the postponed holes; the DATA variant with `postponed === null` appends only the fresh Flight payload). Both share the extracted `createSsrRootComponent` builder so full/capture/resume render the identical tree. Script strategy: `installClientReferencePreinit` (hooked to plugin-rsc's `setOnClientReference` in the virtual SSR entry) upgrades client-reference modulepreload hints to executing head `<script type="module" async>` tags via `ReactDOM.preinitModule` (per-request CSP nonce flows through a module-private ALS — `runWithPreinitNonce` in preinit-client-references.ts, applied internally by the three handlers, NOT exported); `resolveBootstrapOptions` converts the `import("<entry>")` bootstrap into Fizz `bootstrapModules` on explicit `"preinit"` only (head hint + executing end-of-shell `id="_R_"` module script); `entry-preload-priority.ts` serves that entry hint without Fizz's `fetchPriority="low"` and moves it after the head chunk scripts, in the live stream and the PPR capture prelude (#1025), so hydration does not queue behind images. Flippable: `SSRDependencies.headScripts` (`"preinit"` default / `"preload"` = hint-only + inline bootstrap; any other value throws when `createSSRHandler` / `createShellCaptureHandler` is created), mirroring the `rango({ headScripts })` plugin option | `./cache`                   | Segment and response cache APIs: `SegmentCacheStore`, `CacheStoreScope` (the store's `scope` declaration: `"global"`, `"regional"` or `"local"`, read by `router.prerender()` before it warms a route), `MemorySegmentCacheStore` (per-family `maxEntries` FIFO cap, default 1000, evictions unregister tag-index entries), `CFCacheStore` (L1 + optional KV L2), `VercelCacheStore` (Vercel Runtime Cache via `getCache`; SWR `{d,s,e}` envelope stored as a pre-serialized JSON string — one stringify both measures the 2 MB item cap and feeds `cache.set`; reads parse strings and pass legacy object envelopes through — with Vercel ttl = ttl+swr, delete-model `expireTag` tag invalidation, 64-tag / cross-deploy `version` guards, stale-read herd dampening via a short-TTL `{key}:lock` companion key (only the claiming reader gets `shouldRevalidate: true`; the payload is never re-written to push staleness forward); the cache handle + `waitUntil` are injected so the router keeps no `@vercel/functions` dependency, mirroring `CFCacheStore`; both stores keep a PPR shell memo of fresh shell reads and a tag-marker memo PPR shell reads check their markers through (stale-while-revalidate, tag-name hints start the marker reads with the entry read), configured by the `memo` option (`StoreMemoOptions`: `shellMs` default 2000, `shellMaxBytes` default 16 MiB, `markerFreshMs` default 1000 CF / 300 Vercel, `markerMaxStaleMs` default 10000 CF / 2000 Vercel), per isolate for CF and per cache handle for Vercel, with the tag-marker check still run on every memo hit; the invalidating isolate drops its own copies; what other isolates serve for up to one window (a newer capture, a KV-less purge, another Vercel region's invalidations) is on `StoreMemoOptions.shellMs`), `StoreMemoOptions` (type), `KVNamespace`, document cache middleware, cache scope utilities. `CFCacheStore` bounds the JSON read paths (`get`/`getItem`) across all three tiers with latency budgets (`edgeLookupTimeoutMs` for the L1 `match`, `edgeReadTimeoutMs` for the lazily-streamed L1 body, `kvReadTimeoutMs` for the L2/KV read) via one shared timeout primitive; the document path (`getResponse`) bounds `match` + KV but streams its L1 body unbounded and is debug-silent (the `op` union is `get`/`getItem` only). It exposes a per-read `debug` sink (`CFCacheDebug`, `CFCacheReadDebugEvent`, incl. distinct `kv-timeout`, `match-error`, and `body-error` outcomes plus a per-read `markerMs` tag-marker-resolution duration sitting between `matchMs` and `bodyReadMs`) for deployment validation. A stale-path re-put recomputes a shrinking remaining-ttl `Cache-Control` from an internal hard-expiry deadline (instead of restarting CF retention), an L1 read failure degrades to L2 rather than failing, and non-finite latency budgets fall back to their defaults. Tag invalidation (`cacheTag`/`updateTag`/`revalidateTag`, exported from the root) stamps entries with their tags + a `taggedAt` time and checks them against per-tag KV markers resolved through a per-request memo → optional per-colo L1 marker cache (`tagCacheTtl`) → KV cascade; the marker reads inherit the same latency budgets and FAIL OPEN on a KV timeout, so a degraded namespace never turns a hit into a wrongful invalidation. Markers live in the store's own KV (single-store; `tagInvalidationTtl` bounds marker lifetime, `onRevalidateTag` purges cross-colo). Purge mode (`tagPurge`, opt-in): tagged L1 entries carry namespaced entry `Cache-Tag` tiers (`rg:{ns}` / `rg:{ns}:e` / `rg:{ns}:e:{tag}`, written unconditionally), `invalidateTags()` awaits one batched purge-by-tag call (rejects on failure, like a failed marker write), and L1 hits skip the marker lookup entirely — only the request's tag mask and per-request memo are checked (read-your-own-writes); KV L2 and PPR shells keep the marker check (purge cannot reach them). `tagPurge` accepts the credentials object `{ zoneId, apiToken }` directly (normalized through the built-in client, validated at construction) or a custom purge function; `createCloudflareZonePurge({ zoneId, apiToken })` is the underlying chunked purge client (also usable for `onRevalidateTag`). Every read/write failure routes to the router's `onError` via `CacheErrorCategory` (`cache-read`/`cache-corrupt`/`cache-write`/`cache-delete`/`cache-invalidate`/`stale-revalidation`) without failing the request; a corrupt L1 body (genuine parse error, distinct from a transient `cache-read` outage) self-heals — reported `cache-corrupt`, falling through to L2, evicted only when no good L2 copy exists so the evict cannot race the KV→L1 promote. Exported header constants `CACHE_STALE_AT_HEADER`, `CACHE_STATUS_HEADER`, `CACHE_REVALIDATING_AT_HEADER`; error-category type `CacheErrorCategory`. `CACHE_READ_ERROR` (+ type `CacheReadError`): optional `SegmentCacheStore.get` return distinguishing a swallowed backend read failure from a miss — the built-in stores return it from their internal catch (render outcome identical to a miss for plain consumers; the PPR replay composition refuses the seeded doc-record fallback on it, keeping the render-uncached contract). Delegating store wrappers should forward it. Both persistent stores key by per-router versions computed by `vite build` (data version for segment entries and `"use cache"` items: `CFCacheStore` segment entries and `fn:` items, `VercelCacheStore` families `s`/`i`; document version for response and shell entries: `doc:`/`shell2:`, families `r`/`h`), read per operation from the request context (`getCacheVersions()`, public with the type `RouterVersions` so a custom persistent store can key the same way); tag markers carry no version, and a store/router `version` replaces both (see `docs/design/per-app-cache-version.md`). PPR shell caching (axis 2, opt-in via the `ppr` path option): serving is INTEGRAL to the router — no middleware to mount; `path(pattern, Handler, { name, ppr: true | PartialPrerenderProps })` declares the document-level opt-in and its policy (`ttl`default 300,`swr`, operational `tags`, `captureTimeout`ms settle budget default 15000), and the shell store is the app-level`createRouter({ cache })`store via the optional`getShell`/`putShell` `SegmentCacheStore`family (memory/CF/Vercel; reactVersion+buildVersion-gated (`buildVersion`is the router's document version: a deploy that changes the router invalidates like a React upgrade, one that does not keeps its shells) with a pre-commit payload-integrity check, tag-invalidatable, host-scoped keys). The serve path commits AFTER the whole middleware chain; on a HIT the stored prelude flushes first and fizz resumes only the holes; on a MISS a background mixed-chain capture runs (cache()'d segments replay, uncached handlers execute, loaders masked). A ppr route on a store without the shell family degrades to axis 1 with a once-per-key warning; a KV-less`CFCacheStore`runs the shell family L1-only (edge-only ppr: each colo captures/serves its own Cache API shell; tag eviction KV-less needs purge mode, and a tagged shell without`kv`or`tagPurge`warns once per isolate that invalidation cannot reach it; an over-limit tag set is acknowledged `"uncacheable"`from`putShell`so the capture scheduler backs the key off; the store declares`SegmentCacheStore.tagHistoryInert` so tagged BUILD-manifest shells decline instead of becoming permanently un-evictable). The route's`ppr` option also caps the loader pins in the entry's capture data snapshot (`maxSnapshotBytes`, default 8 MiB): over cap the pins are dropped and the doc record kept — shell still stored and replayed, once-per-key report; a whole entry over the store's value limit (`SegmentCacheStore.maxShellEntryBytes`, default 25 MiB, the KV limit) is refused |     |
| `./cloudflare`              | Cloudflare preset integration. `createCloudflareTracing()` -> `RouterTracingConfig` for the router `tracing` option; emits Cloudflare custom spans (`rango.request/middleware/action/loader/handler/render/ssr/response/background`) by wrapping each phase with `executionContext.tracing.enterSpan`, so they nest by async context next to the platform automatic KV/D1/fetch spans. Import-free: reads `executionContext.tracing` lazily (no `cloudflare:workers` import, no `@cloudflare/workers-types` dep); off-Cloudflare or with no wrangler tracing destination every span call is a transparent pass-through. `CloudflareTracingOptions` (`enabled`, per-phase `spans`). | `./vercel`                  | Vercel preset tracing integration. `createVercelTracing()` -> `RouterTracingConfig` for the router `tracing` option; a thin wrapper over `createOTelTracing` that reads the global OTel tracer `@vercel/otel`'s `registerOTel()` installs, emitting the `rango.*` phase spans on Vercel's trace waterfall. Node-runtime only (Vercel custom spans are unsupported on Edge). `VercelTracingOptions` (`enabled`, per-phase `spans`, `tracerName` default `"rango"`, `tracer` override). The Vercel cache store (`VercelCacheStore`) is exported from `./cache`, mirroring the Cloudflare split. The public `./client` client-URL surface is intentionally small:
`clientUrls` and the `ClientUrlPatterns`, `ClientUrlRouteRecord`, and
`OutletState` types. Both client entry conditions expose the same names. There
are no public client-URL middleware or revalidation types in the narrowed API.

`renderRoute` in `./testing/dom` accepts an instance-scoped `defaultPrefetch`
and uses the production delegated-anchor registration inside that test's RTL
container. This keeps Link fallback behavior, basename/static-resource scope,
and the plain-anchor `data-prefetch="false"`/`"none"` plus hard subtree
`data-prefetch-scope="false"`/`"none"` opt-outs reachable through the public
DOM testing primitive without mutating the process-wide browser default.

`renderRoute`'s `hydrate: true` option is how a hook's hydration render becomes
reachable through the public DOM primitive (#992: `useLocationState` inside a
late-hydrating Suspense boundary). It renders the same element to HTML with
`react-dom/server`'s `renderToString`, with `window` and `document` deleted for
that synchronous pass so `typeof window` branches take their server side, then
hydrates the container through RTL's `render({ hydrate: true })`. It also sets
`data-hydrated` on `<html>` after hydration, as the production root does
(`browser/rsc-router.tsx`), so a `<Suspense>` boundary hydrates late by
structure. The result is a `RenderRouteHydrateResult`: `serverHtml`, plus
`recoverableErrors`, the messages React passed to `onRecoverableError` (where a
hydration mismatch arrives). Content that suspends in the server pass is
client-rendered and reported there, not hydrated. The fidelity limit: only
`window` and `document` are removed, so a hook that reads `history`,
`localStorage` or `navigator` outside a server snapshot renders the same in both
passes and can still mismatch in real SSR. Needs `@testing-library/react` 16.2.0
or newer; `renderRoute` throws on older versions, which drop
`onRecoverableError`.

Hydrate mode is also what "a document load" means to the testing surface.
After seeding `history.state`, `renderRoute` with `hydrate: true` calls
`clearLocationStateOnDocumentLoad()` (`browser/history-state.ts`), the function
`initBrowserApp` calls at start-up, so a `clearOnReload` slot is gone before
hydration. A plain `renderRoute` is a client mount and applies every seed.
`clearOnReload` never changes a stored value, only the key, so a seed and the
server primitives' `locationState` are both `{ [Def.__rsc_ls_key]: value }`
for every definition.

`renderRoute`'s `router.navigate(url, { loaders })` seeds loader data for that
one navigation (merged over the render-time seeds), and `RenderRouteSpec`
takes the `transition()` config a node declares. When the chain carries one
(`shouldStartViewTransition`), navigate() commits through production's
`commitInTransition` (both exported from `browser/partial-update.ts` for this
reuse), so a pending Promise seed pins the held reader's
`useLoader().isLoading` exactly as a streaming navigation does. The navigation
lifecycle (`useNavigation().state`, `useLinkStatus().pending`) still stays
`idle`, and production's other hold lanes (same-structure, fully-prefetched,
optimistic) are not modeled: without `transition` the commit stays urgent.

Cache search-param key filtering is exported from both `.` and `./cache` as
`TRACKING_SEARCH_PARAMS` and `CacheSearchParams`. The global
`createRouter({ cache: { searchParams } })` option compiles the filter once per
request in `rsc/handler.ts`; every default cache-key tier applies it through
`cache/search-params-filter.ts` and `cache/cache-key-utils.ts`.

The testing exports also include `PPR_REPLAY_STATUS_HEADER`,
`parsePprReplayStatus()`, and `assertPprReplayStatus()` with the bounded
`PprReplayStatus` / `PprReplayBypassReason` types, and the
`ShellCachePartition` type (`{ keys, generated }`) that `shellCacheKey()`
takes for a store `keyGenerator` partition (#974). `./testing/e2e` re-exports the
same pure helpers for Playwright without pulling the Vite virtual module. A HIT
means an eligible shell snapshot successfully decoded and supplied the partial
match; otherwise the status carries a bounded bypass reason.

The Vercel preset emits `runtime: "nodejs24.x"` by default, matching the
package's Node 24 engine floor. `VercelPresetOptions.runtime` can override it.

### Internal (not user-facing)

These subpaths are consumed by the Vite plugin, RSC handler, or build tooling. They are not part of the public API and may change without notice.

| Export                               | Description                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `./server`                           | Manifest/build internals: plugin bridge, route-map management, router discovery registries, `enableTransitionWhenValidation` (called by the generated routes-manifest module) |
| `./__internal`                       | Internal plumbing shared by build/runtime/Vite                                                                                                                                |
| `./internal/deps/browser`            | Browser runtime dependency bridge                                                                                                                                             |
| `./internal/deps/ssr`                | SSR runtime dependency bridge (`createFromReadableStream`, `setOnClientReference`, `getClientEntryUrl`)                                                                       |
| `./internal/deps/rsc`                | RSC server-protocol dependency bridge (`@vitejs/plugin-rsc/rsc/server`)                                                                                                       |
| `./internal/deps/rsc-client`         | RSC client-protocol dependency bridge (`@vitejs/plugin-rsc/rsc/client`)                                                                                                       |
| `./internal/deps/html-stream-client` | HTML stream client dependency bridge                                                                                                                                          |
| `./internal/deps/html-stream-server` | HTML stream server dependency bridge                                                                                                                                          |
| `./internal/rsc-handler`             | RSC handler internals                                                                                                                                                         |
| `./internal/browser/dev-discovery`   | Browser-only Cloudflare dev stale-document convergence helper                                                                                                                 |
| `./cache-runtime`                    | Cache runtime dependencies                                                                                                                                                    |
| `./types`                            | Type declarations for the `@rangojs/router:version` virtual module (`VERSION`, `ROUTER_VERSIONS`; `ROUTER_VERSIONS` is `undefined` in dev)                                    |

### CLI

The CLI is exposed via the `bin` field in `package.json`, not as a subpath export:

```
"bin": { "rango": "dist/bin/rango.js" }
```

`rango generate` — static/runtime route-type extraction for CI and repo bootstrapping.

## Client API

### Components

`Outlet`, `ParallelOutlet`, `Link`, `Meta`, `Script`, `Breadcrumbs`, and the `Html` namespace (`html.ts`) grouping the document-level components:

| Member                   | Renders                                                                                | Source                                                      |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `Html.Meta`              | Collected `Meta` descriptors + the theme FOUC script, in `<head>`                      | `handles/MetaTags.tsx` (`MetaTags`)                         |
| `Html.Scripts`           | Collected `Script` handle entries for one site (`position`: `"head"` default/`"body"`) | `handles/Scripts.tsx` (`Scripts`)                           |
| `Html.ScrollRestoration` | Scroll restoration across navigations (`getKey`; props type `ScrollRestorationProps`)  | `browser/react/ScrollRestoration.tsx` (`ScrollRestoration`) |

`Html` is `html.ts` imported as a module namespace (`import * as Html`), not an object literal: bundlers drop the members an app never dots into, so a custom document without `Html.ScrollRestoration` does not ship it (an object literal kept it, tripping the cloudflare-basic router-chunk ratchet). `components/DefaultDocument.tsx`, used when `createRouter` gets no `document`, renders all three members, importing each component directly. `html.ts` has no `"use client"` directive, so each member stays the per-export client reference of its own `"use client"` module and a server root layout can dot into `Html` (`<Html.Meta />`). `client.rsc.tsx` imports `html.ts` directly, never via `./client.js`, whose exports are all opaque references in the RSC graph. Pinned by `testing/__tests__/html-namespace.rsc-test.tsx`. The pre-namespace component exports `MetaTags`, `Scripts`, `ScrollRestoration` were removed (no aliases); `ScrollRestorationProps` keeps its name.

| ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |

### Factories

`createLoader`, `createHandle`, `isHandle`, `createLocationState`, `clientUrls`, `href()`

### Deferred handle values — `ctx.use(Handle).defer()`

The push function returned by `ctx.use(Handle)` (typed `HandlePush<TData>`) carries
a `.defer(options?: DeferOptions<TData>)` method for the "decide-sync, resolve-late"
handle pattern. `.defer({ timeoutMs, else })` reserves the handle's slot synchronously
(so the decision lands before the stream seals) and returns a **push-equal resolver** —
same argument shapes as the push (value / `Promise` / thunk), same behavior — that a
deep async component calls later. The always-on timeout (`timeoutMs`, default
`DEFAULT_DEFER_TIMEOUT_MS`, 10s) auto-resolves the slot to `else` if the resolver is
never called, so a forgotten resolve cannot hang the render / response.

**Resolve-by-default:** a deferred (Promise) handle value is RESOLVED before any
consumer sees it — never passed through as a `Promise`. The full render resolves
server-side (`handles/deferred-resolution.ts` `resolvedHandleStream`, wired into
`rsc-rendering.ts`/`handler.ts`/`progressive-enhancement.ts` full payloads + the
prerender bake), so SSR markup and the first sync `useHandle` read are resolved; soft
navigation resolves client-side (`NavigationProvider.tsx` `processHandles` is
await-then-apply — it `await`s each yield's deferred values before `setHandleData`,
HOLDING the previous value for free by simply not touching the store until they
resolve; no pending set, no `useHandle` short-circuit). So `collect`/`useHandle`
always receive resolved `TData` (a deferred resolving to `null`/`undefined` is
dropped; a sync nullish push passes through). The `DeferredHandleEntry` type and the
consumer-side `isThenable` narrowing are removed.
Exported types: `HandlePush`, `HandlePushFn`, `DeferOptions`; exported value:
`DEFAULT_DEFER_TIMEOUT_MS`. `createDeferred`/`withDefer` are internal building blocks.

**Default collect is the identity (lossless):** `createHandle<TData>()` with no
collect now passes the per-segment data through as-is — `TData[][]`, one array per
segment that pushed, in segment order — so a consumer can tell which/how-many
segments contributed. `useHandle` on such a handle is `TData[][]`. Opt into a single
flat list with `createHandle<TData, TData[]>((segments) => segments.flat())` (the
built-in `Meta`/`Breadcrumbs`/`Script` all pass explicit collects, so they are
unaffected). The default `TAccumulated` generic is `TData[][]`. A handle whose
module was never imported (collect unregistered) falls back to the same identity
default and **warns in dev** (`collectHandleData` runtime, folded out of production;
`collectHandle` testing): the fallback is harmless for a handle that wanted the
default, but a CUSTOM-collect handle that failed to register silently gets the wrong
shape, and a `Handle` only carries `$$id` so the runtime can't tell them apart.

## Feature Map by Capability

### Route DSL and Composition

`urls()`, `path()`, `layout()`, `include()`, `parallel()`, `intercept()`, `middleware()`, `cache()`, `loader()`, `loading()`, `errorBoundary()`, `notFoundBoundary()`, `transition()`, `map()`, `route()`, `revalidate()`

`clientUrls()` is a separate, narrowed client DSL exported from `./client`. Its
helpers are `path()`, `layout()`, `loader()`, `loading()`, a restricted
`intercept()` (dot-local named target, `loader()`/`loading()` use only, no
`when`/middleware; module-local origin scoping via a materialization-synthesized
`when`), a `transition()` (ViewTransition classes/name, `viewTransition`,
and a browser-run `when`; path-use position only), and a client-run per-loader
`revalidate()` (loader-use position only; the predicate executes in the
browser and its decision rides the `X-Rango-Client-Reval` header, honored by
synthesized predicates on the materialized loader stubs —
`client-urls/revalidation-protocol.ts`). `isAction` is the same callable
matcher as the server predicate (`isAction()`, `isAction(fn)`,
`isAction(import * as Mod)`, `isAction({ a, b })`), built by
`makeIsAction(actionId)` in `router/is-action.ts` — not a boolean. It requires named client component
values and projects only the `name`, `search`, `trailingSlash`, and `ppr` path
options. It mounts through
`include()` in the canonical `urls()` tree (the composition baseline —
URL/name prefixes, wrapping RSC layouts, and middleware scope derive from the
server tree); `.routes(ClientUrlPatterns)` is pure-client sugar for a root
include.

`include(prefix, patterns, opts?)` takes its second argument two ways: **eager** (a `urls()` value already in the graph, evaluated at startup) or **async** (`() => import("./routes")`, code-split behind a thunk imported on the first request to the prefix, then cached — the split module exposes its `urls()` value — or a `clientUrls()` definition, adapted the same way as the eager client mount — as `export default`). Both are supported; prefer async for large independently-loadable groups. Build-time discovery awaits the provider, so `href()`/`reverse()`/generated types/prerender still cover every route in a split group, including nested `include()`s. Because discovery resolves the provider to build the trie/types/prerender, the `./build` `generateManifest*` functions and `Rango.findMatch` are `async`; provider normalization lives in the internal `urls/include-provider.ts` (`isIncludeProvider`, `resolveIncludeModule`). See [async-includes.md](./async-includes.md).

### Router Lifecycle

Public API (`Rango` interface):

- `createRouter()` with `.routes()`, `.use()`, `.reverse()`, `.fetch()`
- `.debugManifest()` -> `Promise<SerializedManifest>` (type exported from
  `.`): snapshot of each `.routes()` / `urls` mount's routes and layouts. A
  development aid, but not gated: `router.ts` wires it unconditionally, so it
  also works in a production build. Lazy `include()` groups are not expanded
  (`router/debug-manifest.ts` skips their placeholder entries), so included
  routes are absent.
- `clientUrls()` definitions mount through `include()` in the canonical
  `urls()` tree; `.routes(ClientUrlPatterns)` is the pure-client shorthand
  that normalizes to a root include (`include("/", def, { name: "" })`). The
  browser match is presentation-only and the materialized server routes remain
  canonical.
- `routeMap`, warmup handling, document wrapper, global not-found/error defaults
- `strictMode` (default true) — wraps client hydration in `React.StrictMode`; shipped to the client via initial payload metadata and read once by the browser entry. `strictMode: false` opts out (used to isolate StrictMode's double-render when measuring hook stability)
- `prefetchCacheSize` (default 100) and `prefetchConcurrency` (default 2) — client prefetch tuning knobs: max decoded prefetch payloads kept before FIFO eviction, and max concurrent speculative prefetches. Resolved server-side (`router/prefetch-limits.ts`) and shipped via initial payload metadata. The synchronous cache and small shared viewport observer stay eager so navigation can adopt a warm response and detect the first intersection; `browser/prefetch/loader.ts` holds decoder/concurrency configuration and defers evaluating the fetch/queue runtime until an actual prefetch trigger. That deferral is evaluation-only: every `browser/prefetch/` module ships inside the eager `router` chunk, so the dynamic import resolves without a network fetch — the #766 lazy-chunk split created a document -> router -> runtime request waterfall on production's `"viewport"` default and was folded back (`getManualChunks` JSDoc has the numbers). Sub-1/non-finite values fall back to the default; disabling prefetch entirely remains `prefetchCacheTTL: false`'s job
- Respawnable prefetch entries — a decoded prefetch payload is single-render (its handle stream drains during the commit), so adoption used to empty the cache slot: revisiting a route needed a fresh hover-prefetch, and a fast hover-then-click revisit streamed like a cold load. `executePrefetchFetch` now tees an unread reserve branch of the raw Flight bytes before the eager decode; after a clean EOF the entry carries a `respawn` closure (`browser/prefetch/fetch.ts` `makeRespawn`) and `consumePrefetch` re-arms the slot in place with a fresh decode of those bytes — fresh handle stream, chunk imports are module-cache no-ops. The ORIGINAL timestamp is kept, so `prefetchCacheTTL` bounds the age of the data, not of the latest adoption; rango-state rotation still wipes everything. A click that lands BEFORE clean EOF adopts a respawn-less entry (pre-headers inflight adoption or a mid-stream cache adoption) and leaves the slot empty — the completion handler then refills it with a respawned sibling once the bytes prove complete (`hasPrefetch` guard skips if the slot went live again; `storePrefetch`'s generation check drops the sibling after an invalidation). Truncated, aborted, or undecodable streams never arm `respawn` and stay one-shot; evictions release the buffered bytes via `dispose`.
- `defaultPrefetch` (default `"none"` in development, `"viewport"` in production) — router-wide strategy for Links without an explicit `prefetch` prop and intercepted plain anchors inside the router basename.
  Same-page hash anchors stay native and never arm prefetch. Location-dependent
  rejects are parked separately from permanent failures, so a persistent
  hash-only anchor is re-evaluated after navigation without a full DOM rescan.
  A false internal custom delegated predicate result is permanently ineligible;
  only location dependence the router can identify itself is parked.
  Basename and anchor pathnames compare in canonical encoded form:
  Unicode/encoded basename spellings match, but `%2F` remains one out-of-scope
  segment instead of expanding router ownership. `data-prefetch="false"` or
  `"none"` opts out an individual plain anchor; `data-prefetch-scope="false"` or
  `"none"` is a hard DOM-subtree opt-out for both Links and plain anchors,
  including explicit descendant opt-ins and custom delegated predicates. Common
  static-resource extensions are excluded unless `data-prefetch="true"`
  identifies an application route and skips resource decoding/classification
  entirely. Extensionless unsafe GET links still need an explicit opt-out.
  The server resolves the strategy in `router/prefetch-default.ts`, ships it in
  initial payload metadata, and threads it through `navigation-bridge.ts` so
  Link and delegated resolution cannot diverge. `Link` reads it at render and
  subscribes to adaptive capability changes; after hydration,
  `browser/link-interceptor.ts` observes current and dynamically inserted
  eligible anchors. Scope lookup is one ancestor `closest()` check when a link
  arms. Scope mutations notify only descendant delegated anchors and subscribed
  viewport/render Links; removing a scope re-arms them without per-Link
  observers, while adding one cannot recall queued or in-flight work. Delegated
  location notifications revisit only parked rejects; already eligible anchors
  stay armed or completed instead of being parsed and prefetched again after
  every navigation. A completed local prefetch-cache invalidation separately
  re-arms tracked viewport/render anchors under the new Rango-state key without
  scanning rejected anchors or the document. `observer.ts` and adaptive strategy
  caching expose test-only resets instead of carrying test-global identity
  branches in production.
  Per-Link `prefetch` wins over the router default unless an ancestor scope
  disables the entire subtree.
- Named cache profiles via `cacheProfiles`, nonce provider, version tracking
- Per-router cache versions: `vite build` computes a data version and a document version per `createRouter()` from its built code, so a deploy that does not change a router keeps its cache (`createRouter({ version })` overrides both; `rango({ encryptionKey })` keeps routers with inline-action bound arguments stable). See `docs/design/per-app-cache-version.md`.
- Request timeouts via `timeout`/`timeouts`/`onTimeout` options
- `basename` for sub-path deployments — auto-prefixes all routes, `reverse()`, `Link`, `redirect()`, `router.use()` patterns, and `useRouter()` navigation. `href()` is intentionally not basename-aware (raw path helper).

Internal API (`RangoInternal`, not exported):

- `.match()`, `.matchPartial()`, `.matchError()`, `.previewMatch()`, `.matchForPrerender()`, `.renderStaticSegment()`

### URL Typing and Generation

- `route()` macro expansion, `href()`, `href.<format>()`, `reverse()`, scoped reverse APIs
- `GlobalReverseFunction`: the global-only `ctx.reverse` type of middleware and response-route handlers (no `include()` scope, no param auto-fill; `.name` is a type error)
- `ProblemDetails` (RFC 9457) error type and response-route type extraction

### Response Routes

`path.json()`, `path.text()`, `path.html()`, `path.xml()`, `path.md()`, `path.image()`, `path.stream()`, `path.any()`

Response middleware wrapping, automatic content negotiation, bare-value JSON responses, RFC 9457 (problem+json) error bodies.

### Match and Execution Pipeline

URL pattern matching, middleware execution, segment resolution, error matching, route preview, partial matching, handler resolution for full requests, partial RSC, and actions.

### Client URL Discovery and Navigation

A default-exported `clientUrls()` value in a `"use client"` module is recorded by
Vite discovery, evaluated through the SSR runner, serialized without component
implementations, and installed in the server projection registry. The router
materializes ordinary `urls()` paths from that projection; loaders resolve by
their registered IDs, including non-fetchable definitions. Static and runtime
route-type discovery both include named client routes.

After hydration, `client-urls/navigation.ts` supplies a pathname-only local match
to the existing navigation bridge. It can select transient destination
`loading()` and set `useOutlet().pending` for a different matched client route.
The existing partial Flight fetch, global middleware, server match, history, and
commit path remain authoritative. Hard SSR and hydration use the materialized
server projection.

### Data Loading

- `loader()` declarations, `createLoader()`, `useLoader()`, `useFetchLoader()`
- `loader(Def, { ssr: false }, use?)` — per-loader SSR-completeness
  opt-in (`LoaderOptions`, exported from the root). Document renders await the
  flagged loader before segment resolution returns (`LoaderEntry.awaitBeforeFlush`,
  stamped per-isSSR at DSL-evaluation time via the manifest cache key), so its
  data, `ctx.use(Handle)` pushes, and a thrown `notFound()`'s 404 status are
  deterministically in the SSR'd document instead of racing Response
  construction; unflagged siblings in the same segment keep streaming behind
  `loading()`. Client navigations still stream (the flag never lands on
  navigation-lane entries). A flagged loader calling `ctx.rendered()` (or the
  `ctx.get(handle)` read it gates) fails fast — that wait is a barrier cycle by
  construction. Shell-capture renders await flagged loaders too (the bake
  lane; see [`/ppr` → The loader lane rule](../../skills/ppr/SKILL.md#the-loader-lane-rule)).
  Document renders with a flagged loader on the matched chain also auto-raise
  Fizz's `progressiveChunkSize` to `MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (unless the
  `rango({ progressiveChunkSize })` option pins it): the loader was awaited so
  its content ships in-place, and React 19.2 would otherwise outline any
  completed boundary over 500 bytes to an end-of-stream `<div hidden>` + `$RC`
  reveal once the shell saturates the 12800-byte default
  (`createSSRHandler`, reading `ResolvedSegment.awaitBeforeFlush` off the
  payload). The stamp and settled-value delivery also apply to
  `loading(false)` entries and parallel-owned loaders — both already paid
  the pre-flush await and must not re-suspend at the read site.
- `prefetch: false` — `loader(Def, { prefetch: false })` (`LoaderOptions.prefetch`)
  and `loading(fallback, { prefetch: false })` (the `prefetch` option of
  `loading()`, recorded as `EntryData.loadingPrefetch`) keep work out of
  prefetches. A prefetch (partial request with `X-Rango-Prefetch`) skips the
  flagged loaders, and for a flagged `loading()` the entry's handler, loaders,
  orphan layouts and slots (for a layout, every deeper entry), and marks each
  skipped piece `ResolvedSegment.deferred`. The click that adopts the payload
  commits it, shows the fallback and sends one fill request (`_rsc_fill=1`)
  that runs only the deferred work. Server plan and decisions:
  `router/segment-resolution/prefetch-deferral.ts` (`resolveDeferralScope`,
  `PrefetchDeferral` on `InternalHandlerContext._prefetchDeferral`),
  `segment-resolution/revalidation.ts`; stored routes (`cache()`, `ppr`,
  `Prerender`) defer loaders only. Browser: `browser/partial-update.ts`
  (gates, `runFill`), the in-flight fill slot in `browser/pending-fill.ts`.
  `ctx.rendered()` is refused for a deferrable loader on every request kind
  (`router/loader-resolution.ts`). Document-cache keys gain `:prefetch` for
  prefetch partials and skip `_rsc_fill` (`cache/document-cache.ts`). Inert
  in `clientUrls()` groups and `intercept()`; `clientUrls()` `loader()`
  rejects the option in development. Design:
  [prefetch-false.md](../../../../docs/design/prefetch-false.md).
- Loader-level cache (`loader(Def, () => [cache({...})])`,
  `router/segment-resolution/loader-cache.ts`): item-family read-through with
  SWR. A `key()` result is stored as `loader:<id>:key:` plus its URI
  encoding (`loaderKeyFromResult`, #1009), so it never names another
  loader's entry; a store `keyGenerator` result stays raw. The
  `ctx.use(Handle)` pushes of the body and of the loaders it awaits
  via `ctx.use` are recorded on a MISS (`startHandleCapture` with an `accept`
  predicate on the loader body scope, `isInsideLoaderBody`) into
  the item's `handles` blob (`encodeHandles`, as `"use cache"`) and appended
  to the current owning segment on every HIT, stale included; a stale
  revalidation runs on its own loader executor and its fresh pushes are
  diverted into the refreshed entry only. The record is grouped by the loader
  body that pushed, and the replay delivers each loader's group at most once
  per request (`_claimLoaderPushes`, `setupLoaderAccess`): a dependency a
  sibling loader or the handler already ran keeps its live pushes, and a
  later run of a replayed dependency replaces the replayed values in place
  (`HandleStore.pushReplayed`). A `"use cache"` record groups the pushes of
  loaders the function reads via `ctx.use` the same way (`useCacheRecordKey`),
  and its hit replays them under the same claim (`appendHandles`). The entry
  also stores the tags its execution recorded, those of every loader value it
  read included, next to its `cache({ tags })`, so they invalidate it; every
  HIT re-records them (#964; `cache/cache-tag.ts` "Recorded-tag sets",
  design: `docs/design/cache-tags-flow.md`). The per-execution sets run only
  for a request whose match binds a loader cache() (`bindsLoaderCache`,
  `armLoaderTagSets`, `RequestContext._recordLoaderTags`). A loader body's `ctx.use` of a
  cache()-bound loader gets the binding's value (see `execution-model.md`).
  `runLoader({ cache })` (`testing/run-loader.ts`) runs a loader through this
  read-through. The same per-execution sets carry request-identity reads
  (`cookies()`/`headers()`/`ctx.request.headers`/`getRequestContext().cookie()`
  and `.cookies()`/non-cacheable `ctx.get()`, recorded by
  `recordLoaderIdentityRead` in `server/context.ts`; a `key()`,
  `keyGenerator`, `condition()` or `tags()` read records nothing, `runIdentityExempt`). With no `key()` and no
  store `keyGenerator`, a MISS or stale refresh whose execution, or a loader
  value it read, recorded one fails with `loaderCacheIdentityError` and stores
  nothing, whoever started that execution (`recordedIdentityRead`, #972). A
  declared-key entry whose MISS recorded one stores it as an identity mark
  ahead of the value (`markIdentity`), and a HIT restores it
  (`markIdentityRead`) for unkeyed readers. A read that settles after the
  value only refuses the write. Every loader execution also records its
  first identity read, and the runs it read, on a `LoaderRunIdentity`
  (`server/context.ts` `runInsideLoaderRun`, armed or not, in both loader
  runners: `createLoaderExecutor` and the request context's
  `createUseFunction`): a `"use cache"` body's `ctx.use` or
  `getRequestContext().use` of an already-started loader (either runner's
  memo, or a loader-cache binding's value) goes
  through `readStartedLoaderValue` (`cache/cache-tag.ts`) and rejects with
  `useCacheLoaderIdentityError` once the value settles; a later read fails the
  function's write (`assertLoaderReadsClean` in `cache-runtime.ts`, #1011).
- `fetchable` loader mode for cacheable JSON/resource paths
- Client refresh `key` (per-loader refresh groups) and `useRefreshLoaders()`
  (cross-loader refresh groups via `refreshGroup`; reads may carry multiple group
  tags, and the inverted hook takes the group(s) at call time)

### Request Context and Server Helpers

- `cookies()` -- `CookieStore` with `get`/`getAll`/`has`/`set`/`delete`
- `headers()` -- read-only header proxy
- `ctx.request.headers` (every ctx's `request`, one `Request` object) -- an own,
  non-enumerable getter (`guardRequestHeaders` in `server/cookie-store.ts`,
  over `shadowRequestHeaders` in `server/request-headers.ts`) that runs
  `guardIdentityRead` like `headers()` (#976). Installed by
  `createRequestContext` and `createHandlerContext` (a request the router
  builds and matches: the progressive-enhancement re-render, a
  navigation-only capture). The object stays a real `Request` (no Proxy):
  `fetch()` and `new Request()` copy the headers natively without the
  getter, so they don't throw, and they are not guarded (a fetch forwards the
  visitor's `Cookie`/`Authorization`; the docs tell users not to make one in
  a cached body). `clone()` is shadowed to return a guarded clone. A lazy
  srvx `NodeRequest`'s `_request` (Node dev/preview, vercel output) and
  Node's `util.inspect` hook run with the guard off, so srvx's own
  clone/body reads and a `console.log` never count as reads. Router code
  reads headers only through `requestHeaders()`.
  `getRequestContext().cookie()` / `.cookies()` (internal, off the public type)
  are guarded the same way (`guardRawCookieRead`); the cookies() store reads
  the unguarded `_readCookie()` / `_readCookies()`.
- PPR holes are render-defined, not API-defined, and come from loaders only: live-loader boundaries (structural) and promises nested in an `ssr: false` loader's value (masked by shape). Everything a handler produces bakes, as under `cache()` — including a promise it passes under `<Suspense>`, an async server component, and a nested promise in its handle push. To force a hole, put the data in a live loader read with `useLoader` (lane rule: [`/ppr` → The loader lane rule](../../skills/ppr/SKILL.md#the-loader-lane-rule)). During a capture, `cookies()`, `headers()`, `ctx.request.headers`, `getRequestContext().cookie()` / `.cookies()`, a theme read, a `{ cache: false }` variable read, and `ctx.dynamic()` refuse it wherever the capture waits (`guardIdentityRead`, `server/context.ts`); a `key()`, store `keyGenerator`, `condition()` or `tags()` reads freely (`runIdentityExempt`, `cache/cache-exec-scope.ts`), and a cached body, loader body or funnel it starts is guarded again. A hole never reads the shell snapshot: it is dynamic or has its own cache. See `docs/design/ppr-shell-resume.md`. (A `live()` primitive shipped briefly in #641 and was removed in #645.)
- `getRequestContext()` -- full request data server-side, plus shared variable access via `ctx.get()`/`ctx.set()`
- `ctx.build` is true in build-time prerender and build-shell capture contexts, false for live requests. Build-shell middleware gets the same flag and an inert `ctx.waitUntil()` so apps can skip side-effectful runtime work during producer B.
- `ctx.dynamic()` is the request-level PPR opt-out. Middleware calls happen before the shell HIT commit point and force axis 1; handler calls during a MISS suppress the follow-up shell capture. Build-shell middleware calls produce a `dynamic` shell outcome and leave that URL for runtime. It gates the PPR SHELL axis only — a `Prerender()` route's build-baked B-segments still replay at runtime — and is inert in the prerender-collect / static-render contexts. Unit-testable through `runMiddleware`/`renderHandler` (`build` option + `dynamic` result field).
- All guard against use inside `"use cache"` functions

### Search Parameters

Route-local schema definitions (`search` option), typed route param types (`RouteParams`, `RouteSearchParams`), runtime parse/serialize utilities.

### Cache Architecture

- PPR navigation replay is server-only: an eligible partial request seeds the
  captured canonical `doc:` segment record into `matchPartial()`. Without a
  usable snapshot, the first cold request schedules a navigation-only shell
  capture, which settles the handler output and runs the capture guards before
  writing its doc record; later navigation/prefetch requests can replay its
  snapshot. Navigation-only
  captures use a separate shell key, a stripped document request identity, and a
  bounded background queue, so they neither overwrite document shells nor write
  explicit `cache()` scopes under partial keys. Live DSL loaders and their
  `"use cache"` reads stay live; replaying a shell a document request captured
  arms its bake-lane loader seed, so `ssr: false` loaders are served from their
  pins as on a document HIT (a navigation-only capture carries no loader pins).
  The implicit scope keeps consumer `cache()`
  TTL/SWR/store/key/tag semantics authoritative. Intercepts,
  nonce-bearing requests, stores without `supportsPassiveShellReads: true`, and
  unusable snapshots fall open to the ordinary partial path. Production may use
  runtime or build entries; development schedules local background capture and
  never foreground-fetches `/__rsc_shell`.
  `x-rango-ppr-replay` reports whether the seeded segment record actually
  supplied the partial match, including freshness, or why replay was bypassed.
  No Flight resume is involved; replayed segments DO ride the partial payload
  as verbatim `__rangoFragment` envelopes (#700 fragment splice, capability-
  gated and armed per match window), expanded by the client's
  navigation/prefetch decoders before any consumer renders. A fragment decode
  failure retries once without passthrough so server-side eviction and seeded-
  snapshot healing remain intact; the capable document-cache slot is replaced
  with the fallback, the current tab disables further passthrough, and
  context-less clients remain in a separate slot.
- Route-level segment caching (`cache()` DSL), named cache profiles (`cacheProfiles`)
- `cache()` + segment scope propagation, global segment cache config on router
- A route's `cache()` entry holds only the boundary's subtree (`CacheScope.covers`, boundary = outermost enabled `cache()` entry of the chain); a hit resolves the entries above it fresh (`withCacheLookup`). A `ppr` route's scope covers the whole chain (`buildEntriesAndCacheScope`, `route-snapshot.ts`)
- Nested keyed `cache()` scopes (#970): a `key()` partitions every record under its `cache()`. `CacheScope.keyFns` holds the chain's `key()` functions, outermost first (`cache(false)` adds none and does not cut the chain); `CacheScope.resolveKeyFrom` takes their results and, for a scope without its own `key()`, appends its own default key (`resolveDefaultKey`: the store `keyGenerator` result, else the default key), so routes under an inner no-key `cache()` keep their own records; the parts are composed by `composeCacheKeys` (`cache/cache-key-utils.ts`: each `key()` result namespaced as `key:` + its URI encoding (#975), a default part URI-encoded, joined by `|`, a lone default part raw), so no `key()` result equals a default or composed key; each `key()` is memoized per request on `_resolvedCacheKeys`. A scope with its own `key()` skips the store `keyGenerator`. The segment record and the response-route entry (`rsc/response-cache-serve.ts`) key by it; the PPR shell partition and navigation replay use `CacheScope.resolvePartition` (via `resolveShellPartition`): the `key()` results without the default key, which the shell key already carries, plus a `keyGenerator` result that differs from the default key
- Nested `cache()` scopes inherit (#974): `CacheScope.conditions` (every `condition()` on the chain; a read or write needs all, `allowsCache`), `CacheScope.tagOptions` (every `tags` option; `resolveTags` unions them for the record, `recordTags`, the capture doc record and the response entry), and `CacheScope.storeScopes` (enclosing no-key scopes on another store: each distinct `keyGenerator`'s result is a partition part, `resolvePartitionParts`; the parts keep their positions, `positionalParts`: a default-key result is an empty part unless every one is, and an empty result fails key resolution, `generatedPart`). A loader's own `cache()` and `"use cache"` do not inherit.
- `cache()` among a path's children (either form) sets that route entry's own `cache` config, so the route is its boundary and its handler, layouts and parallels are the cached unit; page and response routes alike (`cache()` in `dsl-helpers.ts`). A `cache()` inside a routeless `layout()`/`middleware()`/`transition()` wrapper in a path does the same (`enclosingRoute()`)
- Orphans render the routeless entries in their own `layout[]` (`resolveOrphanLayout`, `resolveOrphanLayoutWithRevalidation`), so a `layout()` after a bare `cache()` in a layout's children wraps every route of that layout; a bare `cache()` that is also a chain entry resolves once, at its chain position (`ResolveSegmentOptions.chain`, `collectRouteMiddleware`)
- `"use cache"` directive runtime wrappers, response route cache layer
- SWR background revalidation re-establishes the request-context ALS (so a cached body reading `getRequestContext()` resolves off the request's I/O context on workerd); profile opt-in `foregroundOnAction` re-executes a stale entry in the foreground during a server action's revalidation render (fresh action response) instead of serving stale + background-revalidating
- Tag-based invalidation: `cacheTag()` (runtime) + `cache({ tags })` (static/dynamic); `updateTag()` (awaitable, read-your-own-writes) and `revalidateTag()` (background, non-blocking — both hard-purge; the only difference is awaitability) fan out to the store-level `invalidateTags()` (the whole tag batch in one call). `cacheTag()` is render-callable: outside a `"use cache"` scope but during a request render it records onto the request's document artifact (`_requestTags`) instead of throwing, so a plain server component tags the PPR shell / document it renders into — PPR's DERIVATIVE invalidation, no first-class ppr tag API (`cacheTag`/`cache-tag.ts`). A route `cache()` record also stores the tags its covered content recorded (render-callable calls and `"use cache"` reads in handlers and server components, `loading()` subtrees included; a loader's tags only when a handler consumes it via `ctx.use()`), is invalidated by them, and re-records them on a HIT — so a shell captured by replaying the record, or a document stored over the HIT, stays evictable (#957; tag owners `runInSegmentTagScope` / `linkLoaderTags` / `recordLoaderTags` in `cache-tag.ts`, loader owner from `getCurrentLoaderBodyId`, handle values encoded under their own owner and `collectRecordTags` in `cache-scope.ts`; armed only when the match resolved a cache scope, `armRecordTagOwners` in `match-api.ts`, and never for a document HIT tail, which writes no record). A `"use cache"` entry also stores the tags of the `"use cache"` calls it makes, from their miss or their stored entry (#980; `recordOwnedTags` in `cache-tag.ts` adds recorded tags to the enclosing `"use cache"` scope and every scope above it, `scopeParents`). Every cache write (`"use cache"`, a loader's own `cache()`, route `cache()` records and response-route entries, the document cache; misses and stale refreshes) is skipped when one of its tags was invalidated after its execution started, in any request of the isolate or per the store's markers for another isolate (#977; the isolate order and `executionStart` in `invalidation-order.ts`, `predatesInvalidation` in `tag-invalidation.ts`, the store half through `SegmentCacheStore.isTagsInvalidatedSince` asked fail-closed, with concurrent gates of a request sharing a marker read in flight, `gateMarkerRead` in `request-tag-mask.ts`, and the isolate order checked again after the store answers; the document cache takes the request start, `RequestContext._requestStart`). Built-in stores index tags; the CF store keeps markers in its own KV (single-store, no companion tag store), and the tag-marker reads inherit the L1/L2 latency budgets and fail open. Explicit `cache({ store })` stores are registered for invalidation via a handler-owned, LRU-bounded registry. Document-cache entries are tagged with the request's tag union; a PPR shell entry with its doc record's tags (a replayed route record's tags reach it through `recordSegmentTags`), its bake-lane loaders' (`SHELL_BAKE_TAG_OWNER` / `linkLoaderTagsTo` in `cache-tag.ts`) and `ppr.tags`, so both are tag-invalidatable. When an invalidated store keeps isolate memos (`CFCacheStore`, `VercelCacheStore`), `updateTag()`/`revalidateTag()` set the fresh-reads cookie on the response (`<state cookie prefix>-fresh`, `rango-state-fresh` by default and shared by the host's routers with that prefix; HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/, Max-Age = the stores' longest memo staleness plus 1 s, `SegmentCacheStore.freshReadsWindowMs`; not set, with a dev warning, once the response was handed off (`RequestContext._responseSent`, a streaming loader or render)); the same user's requests carrying it skip the PPR shell memo and the tag-marker memo.
- Vercel accepts up to 128 tags per item. Ordinary entries use `expireTag`; PPR/build shells additionally use one-year `tm` generation markers, and tagged shell retention is bounded to that marker lifetime so a raced invalidation cannot later resurrect.
- PPR shell caching (the `ppr` path option; `PartialPrerenderProps` exported from the root) — an opt-in second render axis, integral to the router (no middleware to mount). It caches the rendered HTML shell (React `prerender`'s prelude bytes plus the `postponed` resume state, one coupled `ShellCacheEntry`) and, on a hit, commits the composed response after the WHOLE middleware chain: prelude bytes flush first, then fizz resumes only the holes; the browser sees one ordinary streamed document. Holes come from loaders only — live-loader boundaries (structural; only `ssr: false` loaders bake, every other loader is masked at capture — lane rule: [`/ppr` → The loader lane rule](../../skills/ppr/SKILL.md#the-loader-lane-rule)) and promises nested in an `ssr: false` loader's value or a loader's handle push (masked by shape); everything the handler layer produces is shell, as under `cache()`: promises a handler passes under `<Suspense>`, async server components, nested promises in handler handle pushes (`settleNestedThenables`, `router/segment-resolution/mask-nested.ts`), top-level pushed promises, and loaders a handler awaits. The record-first step (`settleCaptureRecord`, `rsc/shell-capture.ts`; outcome `CaptureRecordOutcome`) waits for all of it, bounded by the one `ppr.captureTimeout` deadline (default 15s) that also bounds the prerender; output that does not settle in time stores nothing (no-shell with no in-place retry, the once-per-key warning names the cause), so a partial head snapshot is never stored. The background capture is mixed-chain (cached segments replay, uncached handlers execute) and never re-runs middleware (the derived context inherits post-middleware state). The capture guard (the first step of `guardIdentityRead`, `server/context.ts`, the one guard behind `cookies()`, `headers()`, the theme reads and a non-cacheable `ctx.get()`, which then refuses in a `"use cache"` body, a loader body entered inside one included, and in a `cache()` boundary outside loader bodies) refuses `cookies()`, `headers()`, a theme read, and a `{ cache: false }` variable read anywhere the capture waits — a handler, a promise it passes or pushes, an async server component, a bake-lane loader, and a loader a handler awaits (no handler-invoked loader exemption on this tier; the `cache()` purity guards keep theirs) — and flags the capture context before throwing (`_shellCaptureGuardTripped`), so a caught throw still refuses; `ctx.dynamic()` during a capture refuses it too (the capture context has its own `_dynamic` latch). A normal `ctx.get()` variable and raw `ctx.request.headers` reads are not guarded and bake. Backed by the optional `getShell`/`putShell` store family (memory/CF/Vercel), reactVersion+buildVersion-gated (isValidShellHit; `buildVersion` is the router's document version, so a deploy that changes the router invalidates like a React upgrade and one that does not keeps its shells, openShellDocument rejects corrupt payloads pre-commit, with the HIT's only prelude decode for a `getShell` entry (native `Uint8Array.fromBase64` where the runtime has it; a built-in store's `readShellDocument` hands it raw bytes) and the prelude flushes in 32 KB chunks, a failed HIT tail schedules a healing recapture) and tag-invalidatable. Shell/payload PARITY on a HIT comes from the doc segment record and the CAPTURE DATA SNAPSHOT (`cache/shell-snapshot.ts`, internal). The capture writes its doc record first (`settleCaptureRecord` fires the capture's isolated `onResponse`, so `CacheScope.cacheRoute` Flight-serializes every non-loader segment) and renders its own Flight payload from the record's fragments (`fragmentSegments`), so a server component renders once per capture (before, an uncached async component rendered twice and the prelude and every HIT disagreed). A HIT NEVER runs a handler: `serveShellHit` arms `_shellImplicitCache` with `docTail: true` and `fixedDocKey: entry.docKey`, `resolveShellImplicitCacheScope` returns the implicit doc scope even over a route's own `cache()` scope, and a record that does not hit throws `ShellRecordUnavailableError` (`cache/shell-snapshot.ts`) out of `withCacheLookup`; for a broken entry `degradeUnreplayableShell` (`rsc/rsc-rendering.ts`) then overwrites the entry with a tombstone (which also shadows a build shell), drops the isolate memo, and recaptures, while a merely slow snapshot read (`ShellDocumentRead.snapshotFailure: "unavailable"`, `ShellSnapshotFailure`) leaves the entry alone; either way the response ends with `shellReloadScript` (`rsc/shell-serve.ts`), one reload carrying the forced-MISS marker `SHELL_MISS_PARAM` (`_rsc_shell`), which the handler strips from the request on entry (`withoutShellMissMarker`, keeping the flag `RequestContext._shellForcedMiss` that the serve gate renders on axis 1) and the browser drops from the address bar at boot (`stripShellMissMarker`, `browser/history-state.ts`, called from `initBrowserApp`). The shell's ttl and ttl+swr are capped to the route `cache()` record the capture replayed or wrote (`capShellWindow`, `rsc/shell-capture.ts`, over `RequestContext._routeRecordWindow` noted by `cache/cache-scope.ts`; a record the capture read that ran out mid-capture retries once in place (`expired`), while a second `expired`, no budget to retry, or a record the capture wrote itself ends it with a once-per-route warning; each isolate recaptures a stale shell at most once per `SHELL_MIN_RECAPTURE_INTERVAL_MS`, `staleShellRecaptureDue` in `cache/cache-policy.ts`, which also gates `VercelCacheStore`'s revalidation lock), with a dev once-per-route warning when the cap reduces an explicit `ppr` window (`warnPprWindowCappedOnce`), and a partitioned request that skips an existing build shell warns once, the route probed once (`notePartitionBuildShellCheck`, `hasBuildShell` in `rsc/shell-build-manifest.ts`). The whole-entry size guard measures entries with `estimateShellEntryBytes` (`cache/shell-snapshot.ts`). A route whose record is partitioned by the request (`cache({ key })`, or the store's `keyGenerator`) partitions its shell key too: `resolveShellPartition` (`cache/cache-scope.ts`: `CacheScope.resolvePartition`, the chain's `key()` results composed without the default key (#970), each `key()` resolved once per request on the request context so the capture inherits them and never runs `key()`; a result equal to the default key partitions nothing) and `partitionShellKey`/`navigationShellKey` (`rsc/shell-capture-constants.ts`, re-exported by `rsc/shell-serve.ts`; the partition is URI-encoded so no partition can end in the `:navigation` suffix) for the serve path, its capture, partial replay and the testing `shellCacheKey`. The same React-free leaf owns `buildShellKey`/`shellSearchSeed`, the `x-rango-shell`/`x-rango-ppr-replay` header names and the `PprReplayBypassReason` list (one copy for the serve path and the testing parser), and `warnOnce`, the one registry behind the shell path's once-per-key warnings (reset by the capture, serve and build-shell test resets). The serve gate (`shellServePlan`) renders axis 1 with no capture when the route's own `cache()` refuses the request (`cache(false)`, `condition()` false), and serves a document entry without `docKey` as a MISS except on a Prerender route. A capture with no doc record is refused (prerender-served captures excepted; `settleCaptureRecord` is the one refusal site). A pre-render write barrier settles the foreground's deferred cache writes so the capture replays the foreground's cache generation (never clobbers it); the capture render records the doc record and no cache read (`RecordingShellStore`), stores it on `ShellCacheEntry.snapshot` (required, possibly empty; carried through the CF/Vercel envelopes) with the bake-lane loader pins, pruned to what a HIT reads (`pruneShellSnapshot`: the doc record always; a document entry also keeps the loader-family records; everything else is dropped, `ShellCacheEntry.prunedRecords` reporting what was dropped), and `serveShellHit`'s tail render replays the doc record through the implicit doc scope's segments-only `SeededShellStore` — parity beats freshness inside the shell. A PPR hole never reads the snapshot: a live loader, a promise nested in a bake-lane return, and a bake-lane loader body that runs on the HIT read the store (under the entry's own ttl/swr and #973 masks), while that loader's pinned container paths and its settled handle pushes (restored authoritative, `HandleStore.pushRestored`; its settled pushes on the HIT are dropped, its thenable ones kept) keep the payload equal to the prelude; a HOLE-FREE bake-lane loader record (capture-computed `holes` bit) resolves pin-first and its body does not run on the HIT (or on a PPR partial replay, which arms the same seed once its doc record hits), unless the capture saw a loader push it could not record (`ShellSnapshotLoaderValue.runs`), in which case the body still runs in the background; freshness comes from holes, the shell ttl/swr, and `ppr.tags`. Actions, progressive enhancement, per-request nonce, and `streamMode: "allReady"` (the SEO/bot story) always take axis 1. On a HIT the tail's hydration payload is FRAGMENT-SPLICED (#700): replayed segments carry their STORED per-segment Flight strings verbatim (`__rangoFragment` envelopes, `src/segment-fragments.ts`) instead of being deserialized and re-serialized per request; the SSR resume pass and browser hydration expand them through their own Flight deserializers, so the browser still can't tell. Partial navigation replay HITs are fragment-spliced the same way (armed per match window in `matchPartialWithPprReplay`; the navigation-client payload await and the prefetch decoder expand before any consumer, prefetch-cache entries included). Operability (issue #651): `PartialPrerenderProps.maxSnapshotBytes` (default 8 MiB) bounds only the loader pins (the doc record is exempt): over the cap the pins are dropped and the entry keeps its doc record (once-per-key report; bake-lane loaders then run on the HIT and the record's copies of their handle pushes give way to that run's, `loaderPins` in `router/segment-resolution/loader-cache.ts`; drift repaired client-side); a separate whole-entry guard refuses a capture whose prelude, postponed state, and snapshot exceed the store's value limit (`SegmentCacheStore.maxShellEntryBytes`, internal — `VercelCacheStore` declares 3/4 of its item cap; default `DEFAULT_SHELL_ENTRY_MAX_BYTES`, 25 MiB, Cloudflare KV's value limit); the `debugShellCapture` router option (`ShellCaptureDebug`/`ShellCaptureDebugEvent`, exported) emits one structured event per capture attempt/skip — outcome, barrier/write-settle waits, the record settle (`recordSettleMs`; past 2s it is also named once per key in a dev console warning with the nest / cache() / drop-`ssr: false` remedies), prelude/snapshot/whole-entry bytes (`entryBytes`), queue class/backlog (`queuePriority`/`queueAhead`, also on the `rango.background` span), backoff state — and in dev the terminal event mirrors into the NEXT ppr GET's Server-Timing (`ppr-capture;desc="…"`, plus a `ppr:shell-read` metric and a `ppr:tail` mirror of the previous HIT's per-stage tail timing — snapshot/seed/match/handover/first-html/complete offsets from the commit, in production too when the HIT collected metrics; the HIT's own Server-Timing breaks the store read into `ppr:shell-memo`/`-l1-miss`/`-match`/`-head`/`-prelude`/`-marker` rows plus `ppr:shell-open` and `ppr:shell-commit`, with byte and chunk counts that stay meaningful where workerd's clock does not advance); a KV-less `CFCacheStore` stores shells L1-only (edge-only ppr; a tagged shell with no `kv`/`tagPurge` warns once that invalidation cannot reach it); a custom store can declare `SegmentCacheStore.shellFamilyInert`, which stops captures at the scheduling gate (`skip-inert-store` debug outcome) — no store family or a declared-inert one means the background render is never scheduled, since its write could only no-op. See [PPR shell caching design](../design/ppr-shell-resume.md).
- PPR partial replay freshness (#773): runtime snapshots remain eligible through their SWR window. Partial reads use `getShell(..., { claimRevalidation: false })`; a cold or recoverably unusable URL schedules a navigation-only capture. Fresh build-manifest snapshots remain eligible too. Navigation-only captures carry the full eligibility metadata in a separate shell namespace; partial replay prefers a document snapshot, while document serving never reads the navigation namespace. Navigation-only entries store no document half — prelude/postponed are dropped at putShell (the prerender still runs as completeness arbiter and sanity gate); replay consumes only `snapshot`/`docKey`, and `hasIntactShellPayload` is the document-half gate navigationOnly entries never pass (`DocumentShellCacheEntry` is the narrowed serve-side type). The always-on `x-rango-ppr-replay` response header and `ppr:navigation-replay` metric distinguish an actually consumed fresh/stale segment record from bounded bypass reasons.
- PPR capture queue priority: cross-key renders remain serialized, but a waiting document-shell capture runs before queued navigation-only snapshots (FIFO within each class; the active capture is never preempted). This prevents production viewport prefetch from starving a cold document until `skip-queue-timeout`; navigation captures remain best-effort and retry on later partials.
- Cloudflare runtime PPR shells use Cache API as a per-colo L1 over the required durable KV L2. Both tiers store one prelude-first frame (`cf-shell-frame.ts`: head, raw prelude, snapshot); the document serve path reads it through the internal `readShellDocument`, which resolves after the head and prelude with the tag-marker read overlapping the prelude read, and hands the snapshot to the HIT tail on its own promise (issue #941). L1 miss/error/corruption falls through to KV and a valid KV hit promotes back to L1. Tagged shell L1 entries carry purgeable `Cache-Tag`s but retain the KV generation-marker check even in purge mode because a capture that started before invalidation can finish after the purge and otherwise resurrect.
- Cloudflare shell-tier diagnostics are build-time gated by `INTERNAL_RANGO_DEBUG`. Enabled builds emit compact `[CFCacheStore][shell]` JSON for L1/KV writes, memo hits, L1/KV hits and misses, KV promotion, and marker rejection, including the incoming `cf-ray`/colo plus freshness, expiry, and bounded read timings. Disabled builds emit nothing; the Vite transform folds the flag per environment.
- PPR untagged shell policy: tags are optional. A shell with baked loader material and no render-recorded or static tags follows TTL/SWR-only invalidation without a console warning. Opt-in `debugShellCapture` events expose `untaggedBake: true` on the stored attempt so operators can audit that policy without imposing tags on applications that do not need on-demand invalidation.
- Cached-scope header doctrine (#713): ppr is a document-scoped `cache()` — in any cached scenario only MIDDLEWARE writes response headers. One unified guard (`assertCachedHeaderWriteAllowed`, `server/context.ts`) refuses handler header/cookie/status/theme writes inside a `cache()` boundary AND on any render of a `ppr` route (latched at the segment funnels: positional for `cache()`, whole-funnel for ppr — leaf-entry check, same `isPprEntry` + input as the serve path's `resolvePprConfig`; the intercept funnels carry a defense-in-depth latch off the target route), plus loader writes on ppr routes (headers flush with the shell before loaders settle). Enforced at ONE choke point: a guarded Headers proxy shadowed onto the request context's stub `Response`, so `ctx.header`/`setCookie`/`deleteCookie`/`setTheme`, the handler `ctx.headers` proxy, and raw `ctx.res.headers` mutations all hit the guard at the mutation itself (`setStatus`/`onResponse` stay enumerated; internal serve writers are exempt via the raw Headers). Deterministic first-render throw, dev and prod, one message family naming route + layer + the fix ("set response headers in route middleware"). Deliberate asymmetry: DSL (registered) loader writes inside plain `cache()` stay allowed (they re-run and merge per request — pinned by the `/loader-cookie-allowed` cache-scope-guard e2e + vite-rsc-demo shop cart); a handler-invoked loader body (`ctx.use` from a handler, never registered with `loader()`) throws under `cache()` because it is skipped with its handler on a HIT and its write would land only on the MISS (#725; discriminator `isInsideLoaderScope()` vs `isInsideAnyLoaderScope()`; pinned by the `/handler-loader-cookie-blocked` e2e). Middleware headers/cookies merge into every response including shell HITs (`createResponseWithMergedHeaders`/`applyStubHeaders`, `rsc/helpers.ts`). See the header doctrine section in [PPR shell caching design](../design/ppr-shell-resume.md).
- Build-time PPR shells (producer B, #699): a `Prerender` route that also declares `ppr` gets its complete `ShellCacheEntry` produced at `vite build` and served from the FIRST request after deploy (`x-rango-shell: HIT`, zero runtime capture) — one entry format, two producers, one consumer. The build's shell prerender phase (buildApp post; the prelude embeds the BUILT client bootstrap URL) reuses the discovery temp server, replays middleware with `ctx.build === true` (`ctx.dynamic()` skips that URL), and runs producer A's capture core over the just-collected prerender payloads; entries stage as `__ps-*.js` assets + a lazy `__shell-manifest.js` (pathname-only keys) read through on a shell-store MISS. `ppr.ttl` is staleness-only (recapture = the SWR upgrade path); the buildVersion gate (the router's document version) retires entries when that version changes; `updateTag` evicts by tag-marker comparison (`isTagsInvalidatedSince`, new optional store method on all three stores) against the entry's build-time `createdAt` — no tombstones. Dev parity: the read-through fetches the `/__rsc_shell` dev endpoint (on-demand capture, memoized per HMR generation) for trie `pr`-flagged routes. See prerender-api-design.md (Build-time PPR shells).

### Error and Control Flow

- `redirect()` with optional state and location state integration. Same-origin by
  default: every browser-followed redirect (no-JS PE, full-page GET, middleware
  short-circuit, response-route 3xx) is validated by the server open-redirect
  guard at the single `handler.ts` chokepoint and cross-origin targets are
  neutralized to the basename root; soft SPA/Flight redirects (`X-RSC-Redirect` /
  Flight `metadata.redirect`) are resolved with the same rules at construction
  (`resolveSoftRedirectUrl`). `redirect(url, { external: true })` opts a single
  redirect off-host but only to an `http(s)` target (a `javascript:`/`data:`
  target is neutralized). The opt-in is an out-of-band brand on the Response
  object (`WeakSet`, not a wire header) so a proxied upstream's forged header
  cannot forge it. Shared rules (`redirect-origin.ts`:
  `resolveSameOriginRedirect`, `resolveExternalRedirect`,
  `safeSameOriginLanding`, `resolveSoftRedirectUrl`) back both the client
  validators and the server 3xx/soft paths. See
  `docs/internal/security-checklist.md`.
- Typed error model: `RouteNotFoundError`, `DataNotFoundError`, etc.
- Not-found and error boundary propagation across the route tree
- Loader-thrown authority signals: `throw notFound()` / `throw redirect(...)`
  from any loader (streamed useLoader consumption included). The envelope
  (`wrapLoaderWithErrorHandling`) carries the server-rendered not-found UI or
  the same-origin-resolved redirect target; the client routes them via the
  `LOADER_NOT_FOUND_FALLBACK` / `LOADER_REDIRECT` markers
  (`decode-loader-results.ts` → `StreamedLoaderErrorBoundary` /
  `loader-redirect.tsx`). Document loads get a real 404 status when the
  rejection settles before response construction (opportunistic `_setStatus`);
  loader redirects are always client-side navigations (document-lane 302
  authority stays with middleware).

### Action System

Server action execution pipeline, `useAction()` state tracking, action ID extraction, lifecycle states, server action bridge, action-state UI coordination.

### Route Transitions and Partial Rendering

- `transition({ when })` is a browser predicate ((4) below). The server never
  evaluates it: `router/transition-when.ts` records each matched entry's `when`
  (`_transitionWhenRefs`), `rsc/attach-transition-when.ts` attaches it to a
  response-local segment copy right before Flight, and
  `browser/transition-when.ts` decides each navigation. Stores (segment cache,
  prerender, PPR shell and replay snapshots) never hold it.
- Route-level loading boundaries via `loading()`
- Error/not-found boundary composition
- `transition()` — opts a route into same-route stale-while-revalidate AND (on experimental React) View Transition animation. (1) Content hold (all React versions): a route in a transition scope (itself, or any layout in its matched chain, declares `transition()`) gets a param-agnostic key in `segment-system.tsx` (`inTransitionScope` → `includeParams`), so a same-route param change (e.g. `/product/1` → `/product/2`) reconciles the route subtree instead of remounting it; the `startTransition` wrap `shouldStartViewTransition` already applies (`browser/partial-update.ts`) then holds the previous content while the new loader resolves — no skeleton flash. Cross-route navs remount as before; routes without `transition()` remount on PARAM change (search-only changes hold by default — see the same-structure commit lane below). (2) Animation (experimental React only): the segment content is wrapped in `<ViewTransition>`, so the held same-route swap morphs (`update`/`share`) and cross-route swaps animate `enter`/`exit`; wrap location depends on segment type (layout: default outlet content; route: route component; parallel/intercept slot: slot content). (3) Boundary opt-out: `transition({ viewTransition: false })` suppresses the `<ViewTransition>` wrap (job 2) while keeping the content hold and `startTransition` driving (job 1) — so consumer-placed `<ViewTransition>` elements still animate but rango adds no cross-fade of its own. `createRouter({ viewTransition: "auto" | false })` sets the app-wide default; the per-segment value wins. The global default is resolved into each segment's transition config during resolution (`router/segment-resolution/view-transition-default.ts` `applyViewTransitionDefault`, applied in `fresh.ts`/`revalidation.ts`; only `false` is stamped, unset/`"auto"` is left as-is) so the render gate (`segment-system.tsx`, `transition.viewTransition !== false`) reads the boundary decision off the segment on both server and client without threading the option to the client. (4) Conditional hold: `transition({ when })` (`TransitionWhenFn`/`TransitionWhenContext`/`TransitionWhenKind`/`RouteLocation`, exported) is a BROWSER predicate, decided once per navigation at the first commit that presents the destination: the canonical commit for a server-route push/replace (`browser/partial-update.ts` `decideGatedOff`), the optimistic swap for a `clientUrls()` cross-route navigation (`client-urls/navigation.ts` `beginClientUrlNavigation`, carried to the commit on `tx.transitionGatedOff`), the history-cache restore or popstate commit for back/forward, the action commit and its error lane (`browser/server-action-bridge.ts`), and `kind: "revalidate"` for `refresh()`/stale revalidation.
