Never on the document load, PE paths, or the server. The context is `{ kind, from, to, isAction, action }` with `from`/`to` = `{ url, params, routeName, state }` (`to === from` for action/revalidate); `from` is read from the committed store plus per-history-entry memory (`navigation-store.ts` `rememberDisplayedEntry`/`getHistoryEntryMemory`, keyed by `history.state.key`). The decision ANDs every committed segment's `when` (kept or re-sent, #989), deduped by identity, skipping intercept commits (`collectTransitionWhens`/`decideTransitionGatedOff`); a throw counts as false with `console.error`. A false decision commits urgently for every kind (navigation, `refresh()`, stale revalidation, an action's refetch and its own commit on both the normal and error lanes in `server-action-bridge.ts`, which runs after the response and so outside the transition React opens for a form action) and renders every `<ViewTransition>` with classes `"none"` (`segment-system.tsx` `transitionGatedOff`), so the tree shape and keys never change (#995). A stale revalidation whose history key moved before it landed is discarded without a decision, and a back/forward that opens or closes an intercept is not decided. Payload `metadata.routeName` goes through `publicRouteName` (`route-name.ts`), so internal names never reach `from` / `to`; per-entry memory follows writes to the displayed entry after its commit (`location-state-shared.ts` `replaceCurrentHistoryState` → `navigation-store.ts`). `<Link transition={false}>` / `push(url, { transition: false })` set `transitionGatedOff` without calling a predicate (`navigation-bridge.ts` `navigate`). Transport: in a server `urls()` the value must be a client reference (`"use client"` export, or an inline literal hoisted by `vite/plugins/transition-when-hoist.ts` into `<file>?rango-when=N`); `clientUrls()` sends a when reference (`transition-when-ref.ts` `createClientUrlsWhenRef`) that the browser resolves against the definition (`resolveTransitionWhen`). `applyViewTransitionDefault` strips `when` from the resolved config; `recordTransitionWhenRefs` records it from the static entry chain on every match; `attachTransitionWhen` puts it back on a response-local copy at every payload `segments` field (`full-payload.ts`, `rsc-rendering.ts`, `server-action.ts` revalidation+error-boundary, `progressive-enhancement.ts` full+error). Validation is loud: discovery (`generateManifestFull({ validateTransitionWhen: true })`) fails dev startup, the build and HMR re-discovery (overlay via `vite/router-discovery.ts`) on a server function or non-function, with the route name and pattern (`TransitionWhenError`); the generated routes-manifest module calls `enableTransitionWhenValidation()` so `attachTransitionWhen` throws the same error at render for a route discovery did not see. See [skills/view-transitions](../../skills/view-transitions/SKILL.md).
- Automatic prefetch-driven commit (no-flash, NOT an opt-in): a fully-prefetched navigation — one whose prefetch entry's stream already drained cleanly and decoded (`DecodedPrefetch.complete`, plumbed to `fullyPrefetched` through `navigation-client.ts` → `partial-update.ts`) — commits with `renderSegments({ forceAwait: true })` AND a bare `startTransition` (no `addTransitionType`). `forceAwait` unwraps the already-resolved ROUTER loader data AND the route content promise during render (`segment-system.tsx`: `await loaderDataPromise`, and `await getMemoizedContentPromise(...)` so `RouteContentWrapper`'s `Suspender` renders the resolved node synchronously instead of suspending one microtask), so there is no `loading()`/fallback flash for router data; the transition then holds the current UI across the synchronous resolution so nothing else flashes either. Deliberate trade-off (#622 introduced the transition, #624 reverted it, then reinstated): a CLIENT component that suspends during its FIRST render (e.g. `use()` of a promise created at mount) under an ALREADY-REVEALED boundary holds the old content until it resolves — it renders pre-commit inside the transition, so its effects cannot run first. Boundaries newly mounted by the nav still reveal their fallbacks (React shows new boundaries inside transitions). Cold and partially-prefetched navs (`fullyPrefetched=false`, e.g. a still-streaming or aborted/errored prefetch — `complete` means "decoded + clean EOF", never "stream settled") do NOT `forceAwait`; if they mount new segments they commit normally, so they stream their fallbacks like a cold load. Explicit `transition()` (above) remains the opt-in for the PARAM-nav content-hold and for view-transition animation. The wrapper tree is identical across all commit paths (the `forceAwait` branch only changes whether a promise or a resolved node is passed, never the structural depth — see `docs/tree-structure.md`).
- Same-structure commit lane (default, NOT an opt-in): a plain navigation whose reconciled segments ALL exist in the current on-screen tree by id (`isSameStructureNav` in `browser/partial-update.ts`: `mode.type === "navigate"` + every reconciled id in `getCurrentCachedSegments()`) commits in a bare `startTransition` (no `forceAwait`, no `addTransitionType`) — the action treatment for navigations that mount nothing new. Observable on SEARCH-only navs (filters, tabs): search never rides the segment key, so the subtree reconciles and React holds the visible content while the re-run loaders stream, instead of re-suspending the revealed boundary into its `loading()` fallback for the loader's full duration. Inert for PARAM navs outside a `transition()` scope — the param-bearing key remounts the subtree and the fresh boundary reveals its fallback even inside the transition (the `transition()` opt-in above stays the param-hold lever). `leave-intercept` is excluded (modal close must commit urgently); action/stale-revalidation have their own transition branch. clientUrls pending: `ClientUrlsRoot` reports `useOutlet().pending === true` for ANY in-flight group intent, same-route included (`client-urls/client-root.tsx`), so the held window has a progress affordance. Pinned: `src/__tests__/partial-update.test.ts` (commit lane), `e2e/same-route-nav.test.ts` (plain-product `?tab` hold vs param remount), `tests/vite-rsc-demo/e2e/client-shop-filters.test.ts` (filter hold + aria-busy, dev+prod).
- Transition commit route-state atomicity: `NavigationProvider` calls `EventController.flushRouteState()` inside the same `onUpdate` that schedules the payload, after writing params and any synchronous handle snapshot. The flush cancels the controller's task-debounced notification and invokes subscribers immediately, so React assigns `usePathname`/`useParams` and synchronous segment/handle updates to the payload's normal or transition lane. Browser history still changes at `tx.commit()`, but when a transition holds the source tree, its route hooks keep source values until the destination payload commits; without the flush, the later timer urgently rendered destination pathname/params into the held source UI. The location those hooks read is written only where an entry commits (#1031): `tx.commit()` for a push, a replace and a back/forward that fetches its entry; the restore block of `handlePopstate` (`browser/navigation-bridge.ts`) for a back/forward served from the history cache, next to params and location state and before `onUpdate`; the `revalidate: false` path; and `handlePopstate`'s failure path, in the error boundary's batch. It is not written at the `popstate` event, where it used to be: the page being left is still on screen then, and `usePathname`/`useSearchParams` showed the destination under it for the whole fetch. What still runs ahead of a held tree is a reader that first mounts after `tx.commit()`, and `useNavigation().location` (#1046). Location state does not ride that notification (#1029): it is React state in `NavigationProvider`, set next to `setPayload` in that same `onUpdate` and provided through `LocationStateContext`, so it cannot render with another entry's tree whatever the notification timing, including for a reader that mounts in content a transition is still holding. A commit site hands the controller the entry state it pushed, restored or merged (`EventController.commitLocationState(entryState)`); the controller stores the snapshot (`locationStateSnapshot`) and notifies nobody, and the provider takes it with the payload. So a reader gets an entry's state in the React commit that brings that entry's tree, for a push, a replace, a back/forward (cached restore and refetch) and server-set state on a navigation. Three commits have no payload and pass `treeless`, which marks the snapshot for the provider's own state listener to take with the commit's notification, in the batch that moves `usePathname`: a `revalidate: false` navigation, a commit whose response kept every segment, and a server action's state (same entry; `server-action-bridge.ts` flushes it, and builds it from what readers hold plus the action's slots so a flash value on screen survives). Those three apply to the tree on screen at once; landing while another navigation is still held, they show on the page being left until it commits. `Def.write()` / `.delete()` and the flash clear change history only.
- Parallel slot streaming: `loading()` + `loader()` on a parallel makes it an independent streaming unit (own `LoaderBoundary`, non-blocking across SSR, SPA navigation, and cache-hit paths). Without `loading()`, parallel loaders block the parent layout.
- Slot override dedup: last `parallel()` definition wins per `@slot` name, enabling composition overrides
- Modal/intercept rendering via `intercept()` with `when` config conditions (the match-time selector field of the `InterceptConfig` 4th argument). The selector gets `InterceptSelectorContext` (`server/context.ts`): `from` / `to` are `ServerRouteLocation` (`types/segments.ts`, exported), a `RouteLocation` without `state`, with `routeName` typed `DefaultRouteName | undefined` and filtered through `publicRouteName` (`route-name.ts`) so internal names never reach it. `from` is the intercept source while a modal is open (`navigation-snapshot.ts` `effectiveFromUrl` / `effectiveFromMatch`). A throwing selector does not intercept and is logged (`intercept-resolution.ts` `evaluateInterceptWhen`).

### Location State

- `createLocationState()` -- typed state definitions; each definition exposes `.read()`, `.write()`, and `.delete()` for static (non-reactive) access to its slot in `history.state`. `LocationStateOptions` is `{ flash?, clearOnReload? }`; `flash` with `clearOnReload` throws in `createLocationState` outside production (folded away in a production build, like the missing-key check). All of it lives in `browser/react/location-state-shared.ts`.
  - App version. Location state is versioned by the app version, with no option and no API: a history entry records the version its location state (typed slots and plain `state`) was written under in one field, `__rsc_lsv`, and a read returns only state recorded under the version the document loaded with. You will not find a version in a key or a value. Why a stamp on the entry and not a version in each key: the key is injected at build time and written by the server as well, while the version is a runtime value (the handler's `version` can be set by the app); keys that change per deploy would leave a dead slot per deploy in every entry, and plain state has no key to version at all. The stamp is written by the only three writers (`buildHistoryState`, `mergeLocationState` and `Def.write()`, the last two through `addLocationState`), and checked by the only two readers (`Def.read()` and `useLocationState`, typed and plain, both through `readableLocationState`). A write into an entry another version wrote drops that entry's location state first, because re-stamping it would make the old state readable again; `idx`, the scroll `key` and the intercept fields are kept. An entry without the stamp counts as another version, so state from a release before the stamp is dropped once; a release before the stamp (a rollback) ignores it and reads values as it always did.
  - Which version: the one the document loaded with (`setLocationStateVersion`, called by `initBrowserApp` from the payload's `metadata.version`), not `getAppVersion()`. They differ in development, where an RSC edit bumps the app version inside a running page (`bridge.updateVersion`): comparing against the live version would drop the session's state on every server-module save. With the document-load version an HMR bump keeps it and the next document load drops it, which is what a deploy does. A client without a version (a `renderRoute` tree, which resets it) writes no stamp and reads only unstamped entries, so test seeds and the server primitives' `locationState` need none.
  - Storage key. The value is always stored raw; `clearOnReload` is a suffix on the key the Vite plugin injects: `<key>~r` (`Def.__rsc_ls_key` returns it). Why the key and not a wrapper around the value: slots outlive deploys, and a stored format would have to be understood by every release that ever reads the slot. With the key, a release without the option (a rollback included) and a definition without it read the plain key and never see such a slot; a definition without options runs the same read and write as before the option existed. Collision-free because an injected key ends in `#<ExportName>` (`vite/plugins/expose-id-utils.ts` `makeStubId`; only identifier exports are keyed) and `~` is not an identifier character, so the first `~` after the last `#` always starts a suffix; `withLocationStateKey` rejects `~` in a name. The prefix, its predicate and the suffix are `LOCATION_STATE_KEY_PREFIX`, `isLocationStateKey` and `CLEAR_ON_RELOAD_KEY_SUFFIX`.
  - `clearOnReload` -- the slot does not survive a document load of its entry. `clearLocationStateOnDocumentLoad()` (`browser/history-state.ts`) removes every `~r` key from the current entry, by key alone because at start-up the defining module may not be loaded; `initBrowserApp` (`browser/rsc-router.tsx`) calls it in its synchronous prefix, before the payload is decoded, the store records the entry, or anything hydrates. Nothing is timed per reader: a reader in a late-hydrating boundary, a reader mounted later and a navigation back to the entry all find the slot gone. Server-set state cannot be dropped by it: a document response carries no location state (`rsc/rsc-rendering.ts` attaches it to partial payloads only), and navigation payloads, action payloads and `LoaderRedirect` write after start-up. Client mounts, back/forward and server-set state are unchanged, and a bfcache restore runs none of this. A slot stored before the definition adopted the option is under the plain key: not read, not removed.
- `useLocationState()` -- reactive hook (`browser/react/location-state.ts`). It reads `LocationStateContext`: the snapshot of the entry on screen that `NavigationProvider` holds as React state (see "Transition commit route-state atomicity" above), so the hook has no state, ref or subscription of its own. `useSyncExternalStore` is still called, with a no-op subscription, for its server snapshot only: the hook renders `undefined` on the server and on every hydrating render, late Suspense boundaries included. The snapshot holds the entry's typed slots and plain `state`, only when recorded under the client's version (`readableLocationState`); `locationStateSnapshot` keeps a slot's value, and the whole snapshot, identical when a commit passes back the value readers already hold (no state after no state, a primitive, the reader's own object carried forward, a slot an action did not touch), and structured-clones anything else. Equal content in a new object is a new value on purpose: a link clicked twice announces its flash message or scroll target twice. Does NOT update on static `.write()` / `.delete()`, for a reader that mounts later either. A flash value stays in the snapshot after its reader cleared it from history, until the entry's state is next committed. Inside an optimistic `clientUrls()` branch the hook reads `OptimisticLocation.state`, the entry state the navigation will push (not a copy). Outside a `NavigationProvider` the context is `undefined` and so is every read; history is not read in its place
- `redirect()` integration with location state
- Serializability check: `ValidateLocationState<T>` rejects values `history.state` cannot structured-clone; the `LocationStateUnsafe<reason, path>` brand names each failing field (`items[].info.values`; an object's own unsafe fields first, so a DOM node stops at its methods; depth-bounded at 8)
- `state` on `router.push()` / `router.replace()` / `<Link state>`: `HistoryState` = `readonly LocationStateEntry[] | PlainHistoryState` (both exported from `./client`); a bare entry, an uncalled definition, or an array mixing entries with plain values is a compile error and, in development, a runtime error (`resolveNavigationState` in `browser/history-state.ts`, folded out of production). `PlainHistoryState` checks the top-level value only (plus array/`Map`/`Set` elements): plain object members, and a top-level React element or DOM node, are not checked
- Missing key: a definition without the plugin-injected key throws outside production (dev and test); unit tests key it with `withLocationStateKey` from `./testing`

### Handle Data

`createHandle`, `useHandle`, handle propagation from route handlers into client components, segment ordering and reconciler. Built-in: `Meta` handle for head tags (rendered by `<Html.Meta>`), `Script` handle (+ `<Html.Scripts>` renderer) for injecting nonced scripts into head/body, `Breadcrumbs` handle for breadcrumb navigation.

- **Loader handle writes**: `ctx.use(SomeHandle)({...})` in a LOADER body is
  the push (handler parity); the rendered()-gated READ moved to
  `ctx.get(handle)`. Pushes attribute to the loader's owning segment
  (`_currentSegmentId` pinned at the kickoff sites in
  `segment-resolution/fresh.ts` + `revalidation.ts` — an id outside
  matched/segmentOrder is silently dropped by `collectHandleData`). Delivery is
  async by the race model: the handle store has TWO settlement lanes
  (`handle-store.ts`: `track` = handlers, `trackAuxiliary` = DSL loader bodies;
  `settled` vs `fullySettled`) so streaming loader pushes stay legal without
  blocking SSR/hydration (both drain the document handle stream in blocking
  positions) or deadlocking `ctx.rendered()`. Document lane: pushes that beat
  the handler barrier ride the SSR snapshot; later ones stream via
  `metadata.handlesLate` (`streamLate()`), applied post-hydration behind the
  hydration-commit barrier in `rsc-router.tsx` (applying earlier mutates state
  `useHandle` initializers read mid-hydration — mismatch). A PPR shell HIT
  has no race: `serveShellHit` freezes the document lane at the record's
  state (`freezeDocumentSnapshot`), so the client hydrates with what the
  prelude was rendered from and every loader push of the request is late
  (#1035). A reader React is hydrating reads the handle state the document
  was rendered with (`freezeHydrationHandleState` /
  `getHydrationHandleState` on the event controller, `useHandle`), so a
  boundary that hydrates after the late channel applied an update still
  matches its HTML. Nav/action lanes:
  the payload `handles` generator now streams to `fullySettled`, applied
  progressively by `processHandles`. `loader(Def, { ssr: false })` upgrades
  a loader's handles to guaranteed-SSR: document renders await it before first
  flush (`LoaderEntry.awaitBeforeFlush`), so its pushes beat the barrier
  snapshot. The earlier `stream` option throws at definition time
  (`loader()` in `route-definition/dsl-helpers.ts`). Userland:
  `runLoaderResult().handlePushes` records writes; `runLoader` seeds reads via
  `{ handles }` + `ctx.get`. `cache()` and PPR shell records exclude DSL-loader
  pushes (`handle-store.ts` push-time positional tagging; the shell capture
  untags every loader body's settled pushes (an `ssr: false` loader's own and
  those of the loaders it awaits) and records their loader in
  `CachedEntryData.handleOwners`; a replay restores the pushes of a loader it
  serves from its pin through `HandleStore.pushRestored`, where they stand
  against the settled pushes of a run of that loader on the replay (made in
  its body or replayed from a cache entry inside it), on a document HIT and
  a client navigation alike; every other owner's, a live-lane loader's and a
  loader's whose pin the entry lost, go through `pushPlaceholder` as
  placeholders its run or its own `cache()` entry replaces; see
  `docs/design/caching.md` and `docs/design/handle-push-ownership.md`).

### Revalidation

- `revalidate()` DSL primitive
- Segment-level revalidation defaults, request-method aware behavior
- Custom revalidate callback composition, SWR background revalidation
- `ctx.isAction(...refs)` on the revalidate predicate context — typed,
  rename-safe action matching by reference (single, variadic, `import * as`
  namespace, `{ action1, action2 }`, or grouped namespaces); resolves the
  same id (`$id ?? $$id`) as the action boundary, so it matches in dev and
  production. Called with no arguments it answers "is this an action at
  all?" — true for any in-flight action, false on plain navigation. Shared
  helper: `makeIsAction` in `router/is-action.ts`. The same matcher is
  passed to `clientUrls()` `revalidate()` predicates (browser match is the
  stub's hashed `$$id`). Public types: `ActionRef`, `IsActionFn`.

### Progressive Enhancement

Internal: `handleProgressiveEnhancement()` (in `src/rsc/progressive-enhancement.ts`, not re-exported from `./rsc`) handles no-JS form submission, form-state encoding/decoding for `useActionState()`.

### Cross-tab Invalidation

Public: `invalidateClientCache()` (root entry, both seats) forces the client's caches to miss after a mutation the router can't see.

Internal: the rango state lives in a session cookie (`src/browser/rango-state.ts`), so cross-tab value sync is the shared cookie jar, read on every fetch. The jar-divergence observer (`src/browser/navigation-store-handle.ts`) marks the history cache stale when a sibling tab or a server `Set-Cookie` rotates the value; the `BroadcastChannel` in `navigation-store.ts` still pushes action-driven invalidation to tabs sharing a segment. Its message carries the sender's rotated state and resolved cookie name so only the same router adopts a newer value, then clears locally without rotating the shared cookie again.

### Theming

Router option `theme`, `ThemeProvider` integration on server and client, `ThemeScript` generation, FOUC prevention, cookie-based persistence.

The visitor's theme reads (the handler and middleware `ctx.theme`, `getRequestContext().theme`) are read-only, non-enumerable getters guarded like `cookies()` (#971, `readGuardedTheme` in `server/cookie-store.ts`, over `guardIdentityRead` in `server/context.ts`; getters in `router/handler-context.ts` `THEME_DESCRIPTOR`, `router/middleware.ts` `MIDDLEWARE_THEME_DESCRIPTOR`, `server/request-context.ts`). Non-enumerable so dev Flight's debug serialization of a ctx passed as a server component prop is not a read. A read refuses a `ppr` shell capture (the guard records `_shellCaptureGuardTripped = { surface, fix }` and the once-per-key refusal warning prints both; `cookies()`/`headers()` record theirs the same way), and throws inside a `cache()` boundary or a `"use cache"` body, with the same loader-body exemptions as `cookies()`. The router's own read is `payloadInitialTheme` (`rsc/full-payload.ts`, over the unguarded internal `_readTheme()`, itself non-enumerable so the fetchable-loader ctx's `{ ...reqCtx }` spread in `rsc/loader-fetch.ts` cannot carry it), used for `metadata.initialTheme` by the full and PE payloads and for `ShellCacheEntry.initialTheme`: a capture carries the no-cookie `defaultTheme`, so a HIT never hands one visitor's theme to `useTheme()` for another. A render whose response opted in to the document cache before `next()` carries it too (#978): the middleware marks the render it may store (`_documentCacheRender`, `cache/document-cache.ts`) and `documentCacheStoresRender` checks the response stub against the write's own `shouldCacheResponse`. Any other render that emits a non-default visitor theme marks `_payloadVisitorTheme`, and `shouldCacheResponse` refuses to store that response (a `Cache-Control` written after `await next()` arrives after the payload). The unmatched-route 404 (`rsc/handler.ts`) reads `_readTheme()` directly: it is never stored, and its stub is still a 200 when the payload is built. `ctx.setTheme()` is a response write, refused on `ppr`/`cache()` routes by the #713 header guard.

### Prerender and Build-time Pre-rendering

- `Prerender()`/`Static()` handler types, `BuildContext`, `GetParamsContext`.
  Parallel slots accept Static definitions through the internal opaque,
  handler-less `StaticHandlerRef` seam so descriptor arrows retain contextual
  `ctx` typing.
- Pre-render manifest generation, intercept pre-render artifacts
- Runtime prerender cache lookup flow
- `Passthrough(prerenderDef, liveHandler)` wrapper for live runtime fallback
- `ctx.passthrough()` per-param artifact skip (defers to Passthrough live handler)
- `PRERENDER_PASSTHROUGH` sentinel, `isPrerenderPassthrough()` type guard
- `buildEnv` Vite plugin option for build-time `ctx.env` access (KV, D1, etc.)
- `"auto"` mode calls `wrangler.getPlatformProxy()` for Cloudflare presets,
  with the wrangler config found upward from the Vite root (not `process.cwd()`)
  and persisted state under the Vite root's `.wrangler/state/v3`
  (`wranglerProxyOptions` in `vite/router-discovery.ts`)
- Applies to both production build and dev `/__rsc_prerender` evaluation
- Dev `/__rsc_prerender` memoizes rendered payloads between HMR edits, keyed by
  router-instance identity (`vite/discovery/dev-prerender-cache.ts`, issue
  #654): per-request entry re-import makes instance identity the HMR
  generation (on cloudflare the temp-runner re-import also fixes
  handler-only-edit staleness); one render warms main + intercept variant
  keys; `x-rango-prerender-cache: HIT | MISS` response header
- Build-time render errors surface to the build instead of baking an error page
  (issue #587): `ResolveSegmentOptions.throwOnError` (set only by the prerender
  path) re-throws through `matchForPrerender`; a component that throws while
  the tree is encoded is collected through Flight `onError` and re-thrown the
  same way (issue #914). `prerender.onError` Vite plugin
  option (`"fail"` default | `"warn"`) chooses fail-the-build vs. warn-and-skip;
  `throw new Skip()` inside a render fn skips a single URL/handler

### On-demand Prerender (ISR)

- `router.prerender({ env, ctx })` binds the runtime and returns a runner;
  `runner(target, { onlyIfStale?, throwOnError? })` performs a requestless
  refresh from fetch, cron, queues, workflows, webhooks, or server actions.
  `runner.many(targets, { concurrency?, ... })` adds bounded concurrency and
  `runner.markStale(tags)` marks durable entries stale (marking only: they keep
  serving). Types: `PrerenderRuntime`, `PrerenderRunOptions`,
  `PrerenderManyOptions`, `PrerenderRunner`, `PrerenderFn`.
- `Prerender(..., { onDemand })` is the explicit route opt-in
  (`onDemand: true | { ttl?, tags?: string[] | (target) => string[] }`). Any
  truthy spelling works: producer retention and the runtime `od` trie flag are
  both derived from the evaluated route manifest (`state.onDemandHandlerIds`).
  Combining `onDemand` with the `ppr` path option throws at route definition.
- The `prerender` router option resolves a `PrerenderConfig` per request or call:
  `{ store, ttl?, onRevalidate? }`. The presence of `onRevalidate` is the
  stale-while-revalidate opt-in; it runs once per stale key per isolate while
  one is in flight (`cache-lookup.ts` `scheduleOverlayRevalidation`).
- Serving checks the writable overlay before the bundled manifest, on GETs and
  on server-action re-renders of plain on-demand routes (an action re-render
  re-sends the route's own segments from the overlay). Passthrough routes
  re-render live on actions. A stale overlay entry still serves because it is
  newer than the build artifact; staleness only schedules refresh work.
- The producer reuses `matchForPrerender` without inheriting request state.
  Personalized reads map to `skipped-personalized`; failed renders and writes
  leave the previous entry intact. Its context carries the router's cache
  versions (`_versions`), so `getCacheVersions()` inside a refresh answers like
  a live request.
- Stores are plain get/set (`WritablePrerenderStore`): the trigger composes the
  `PrerenderStoredEntry` envelope and the serve path and `onlyIfStale` read
  verify every answer (shape, `key.version`, params collision guard on the
  32-bit param hash). Keys carry the router's data version
  (`resolvePrerenderVersion`, shared by the trigger and `rsc/handler.ts`), so a
  client-only deploy keeps refreshed pages.
- `@rangojs/router/prerender` exports the in-memory store and public contracts;
  `@rangojs/router/prerender/cloudflare` exports the Cloudflare KV adapter.
- Main and intercept variants remain separate. V1 refreshes the main variant;
  an older bundled intercept artifact can remain until the next deploy.
- Userland testing: `router.prerender()` then `serveShellRequest(router, url)`
  (`@rangojs/router/testing/flight`) serves the refreshed entry through the
  production handler (`testing/__tests__/on-demand-prerender.rsc-test.tsx`).

### Warming Any Route (router.prerender() for every route)

- One verb, dispatched after the route match
  (`prerender/create-prerender-trigger.ts`): a `Prerender(..., { onDemand })`
  route takes the requestless render above and then one warm request; every
  other route is warmed. Each result carries `path: "on-demand" | "warm"`.
- A warm is a cookie-free `GET` (`accept: text/html` only) of the URL a visitor
  requests, dispatched in process through `router.fetch` and marked through a
  `WeakMap` on the `Request` object (`prerender/warm-request.ts`,
  `RequestContext._prerenderWarm`). In replace mode `isWarmReplace(ctx)` makes
  every runtime cache read answer a miss: route `cache()`
  (`CacheScope.lookupRouteDetailed`), loader `cache()` (`executeLoaderData`),
  `"use cache"` (`registerCachedFunction`, which also leads its own execution
  instead of joining one), the PPR shell (`shellServePlan`), the document cache
  and a response route's cache. Each write goes through the unchanged write
  path and replaces the entry; nothing is evicted first.
- The warm's shell capture is forced (`ShellCaptureDescriptor.force`): it
  bypasses the per-key in-flight dedup and the refused-capture backoff, takes
  no `skip-stored` sequence, reads its caches normally (so it replays what the
  warm just wrote) and waits longer on the write barrier. Correctness guards
  are unchanged: identity reads, the tag-invalidation write gates, render
  errors, size limits, `cache(false)` / `condition()`, the document cache's
  refusals, queue capacity.
- `SegmentCacheStore.scope` (`CacheStoreScope`) gates a warm
  (`cache/store-scope.ts` `resolveWarmStoreScope`): `CFCacheStore` with KV is
  `"global"`, without KV `"local"`; `VercelCacheStore` `"regional"`;
  `MemorySegmentCacheStore` `"local"`, counted as shared only under the Vite
  dev server; a store that declares nothing is `"local"`. A local store returns
  `skipped-store-not-shared` before anything renders and warns once per router
  in dev.
- Origin: the target's own, else `PrerenderRuntime.origin`, else the origin of
  the request the runner is called from, else `skipped-no-origin`. A warm
  target keeps its search params; a hash or a reserved param is
  `skipped-unsupported-target`.
- Called from inside a request, a warm runs in the async context that request
  entered the handler with (`captureRequestEntryContext`,
  `RequestContext._runAtRequestEntry`), not in the caller's scopes.
- Result: `warmed` | `already-fresh` (`onlyIfStale`, which reads normally and
  tops up what is cold or stale) | `skipped-store-not-shared` |
  `skipped-no-origin` | `no-store` | `skipped-personalized` |
  `shell-not-stored` | `skipped-uncached` | `render-failed`, with
  `caches: PrerenderWarmCaches` (`writes` by store family, `shell`, `refusal`,
  `document`). `ShellCaptureDebugEvent` gains `refusal`
  (`ShellCaptureRefusal`).
- Not warmed: navigation (`partial:`) and intercept records; other edge
  locations' own copies (a content refresh is `updateTag()` then the warm); an
  app entry that builds its own `createRSCHandler({ cache, version })`.
- Userland testing: `router.prerender()` then `serveShellRequest(router, url)`
  (`testing/__tests__/prerender-warm.rsc-test.tsx`,
  `prerender-warm-layers.rsc-test.tsx`); `serveShellRequest` gives
  `router.fetch` its HTML stub (`rsc/ssr-module-loader.ts`). Design:
  `docs/design/prerender-every-route.md`.

### Request Timeouts

- `timeout` router option — shorthand number (ms), applies to `actionMs` + `renderStartMs`
- `timeouts` router option — structured `{ actionMs?, renderStartMs?, streamIdleMs? }`, overrides shorthand. `streamIdleMs` (opt-in; the shorthand does not apply) bounds end-to-end idle flow on streamed bodies via the rsc/stream-idle.ts watchdog at the handler's response tail: on trip the body errors with RouterTimeoutError("stream-idle"), the source render is canceled, and the trip reports via onError + request.timeout (customHandler always false — onTimeout cannot apply mid-stream)
- `onTimeout` router option — custom callback returning a `Response` for timed-out requests
- `RouterTimeoutError` — custom error class with `phase` and `durationMs`
- `withTimeout()` — `Promise.race` helper returning discriminated union
- `isTimeoutEnabled(ms)` — a phase is active only when `ms` is a positive number (`undefined`/`<= 0` = pass-through); shared by `withTimeout` and the render-diagnostics gate so a `renderStartMs: 0` opt-out disables both together
- Default 504 response with `X-Rango-Timeout-Phase` header
- `onError` receives timeout errors with `metadata: { timeout: true, phase, durationMs, render? }`; `render` is the foreground Flight/HTML/response cursor when a render-start timeout interrupts the stage driver
- `onTimeout`, `request.timeout`, and `onError` each receive their OWN shallow copy of the `render` snapshot (`RenderTimeoutContext`: mode, phase, running/paused state, completed/total, partial phase duration) — value-equal, independent by reference, so a consumer mutating one surface's copy cannot corrupt the others
- `dispatch()` mirrors response-route `renderStartMs`/`onTimeout`/timeout telemetry through the public testing entry; its timeout context deliberately has no `render` snapshot because dispatch does not run Flight/HTML
- Timeout phases: `"action"` (server action execution), `"render-start"` (RSC render / response routes), `"stream-idle"` (post-handoff body idle-flow watchdog; onTimeout does not apply — the trip errors the stream and reports via onError with `metadata: { timeout: true, phase: "stream-idle", durationMs }` + the request.timeout event)

### Telemetry and Observability

- `telemetry` router option — pluggable `TelemetrySink` for structured lifecycle events
- `createConsoleSink()` — development logger for every `TelemetryEvent` variant (11 today, incl. request.timeout and request.origin-rejected)
- `createOTelSink(tracer)` — OpenTelemetry **event** adapter: maps the discrete-fact events (handler error, cache/revalidation decisions, timeout, origin-rejected) to instant `rango.*` spans. Does NOT emit request/loader phase spans (those are the `tracing` slot's, via `createOTelTracing`) — so running it alongside a tracing adapter does not duplicate phase spans
- Event types: `request.start/end/error`, `loader.start/end/error`, `handler.error`, `cache.decision`, `revalidation.decision`, `request.timeout`, `request.origin-rejected`
- Zero overhead when no sink is configured (no-op singleton)
- Structurally typed OTel interfaces (`OTelTracer`, `OTelSpan`) — no `@opentelemetry/api` dependency
- `tracing` router option — span wrapping for the request/middleware/action/handler/loader/render/ssr/response/background phases via a platform `SpanRunner`; routed through the internal `observePhase()` primitive (instrument.ts) which co-emits the debugPerformance perf metric, so spans and the perf timeline are one model. The per-segment `rango.handler` span is span-only (`handler:<id>` perf row owned by `track()`), emitted via the `observeHandler` fast-path that allocates nothing when tracing is off. Pass-through (`NOOP_TRACE_SPAN`) when unset
- `createCloudflareTracing()` (`@rangojs/router/cloudflare`) — emits Cloudflare custom spans (`rango.*`) by wrapping each phase with `executionContext.tracing.enterSpan`, so they nest by async context and appear next to the platform's automatic KV/D1/fetch spans; import-free (no `cloudflare:workers` import, no `@cloudflare/workers-types` dependency)
- `createOTelTracing(tracer)` — OpenTelemetry **phase-span** adapter for the `tracing` slot: bridges the phases onto `tracer.startActiveSpan` (callback-bound, faithful async-context nesting). `OTelTracingOptions` (`enabled`, per-phase `spans`)
- `createVercelTracing()` (`@rangojs/router/vercel`) — thin wrapper over `createOTelTracing` that reads the global OTel tracer `@vercel/otel`'s `registerOTel()` installs (Node runtime only; Vercel custom spans are unsupported on Edge). `VercelTracingOptions` (`enabled`, per-phase `spans`, `tracerName` default `"rango"`, `tracer` override)
- `TracingToggleOptions` — the shared `{ enabled?, spans? }` option pair (exported from the root). `OTelTracingOptions` and `CloudflareTracingOptions` are aliases of it; `VercelTracingOptions` and `RouterTracingConfig` extend it — so a phase added to `TracePhaseToggles` propagates to every factory from one declaration

### Dev and HMR

`rango()` plugin discovery, named-route generation, manifest virtual modules, parser/runtime route-type fallback, lazy loader id injection, duplicate plugin detection. In Cloudflare dev, successful discovery advances a worker generation epoch only when the path, name, trailing-slash, or search-schema shape changes; after invalidating workerd, the plugin probes until the active router reports that epoch, then broadcasts readiness over the browser hot channel. Each document also queries the latest acknowledged epoch at startup and after reconnecting. Only an older document reloads, so content-only `rsc:update` keeps navigation and client state. `poke()` — dev-only Vite plugin that triggers a full browser reload from terminal input: `Ctrl+R` when available, plus safe line-based shortcuts like `e + Enter`.

---

## Architecture Map

```
App Authoring ──> Router ──> Runtime ──> Rendering ──> Client
                    │                       │
                    └── Cache ──────────────┘
                    │
Tooling ────────────┘
```

| Layer         | Source                                    | Responsibility                                                                                                    |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| App authoring | `src/route-definition/*`, `src/router.ts` | Compile route DSL into manifest entries for `router.match()`                                                      |
| Router        | `src/router/*`, `src/server/context*`     | Manifest cache, middleware execution, segment pipelines, error handling, action context, revalidation             |
| Rendering     | `src/rsc/*`, `src/ssr/*`                  | Stream RSC payloads, execute server actions/loaders/response routes, emit HTML with bootstrap and flight payloads |
| Client        | `src/browser/*`                           | UI state via NavigationStore, links, prefetch, router actions, server-action bridges                              |
| Tooling       | `src/vite/*`, `src/build/*`               | Route typings/manifests, plugin/version/runtime metadata, HMR consistency                                         |
| Cache         | `src/cache/*`                             | Cache scopes + stores for segment responses and response routes with SWR semantics                                |
| Extensions    | `src/theme/*`, `src/host/*`               | Theme system, domain-based multi-app composition                                                                  |

---

## Optional / Advanced Features

- Cloudflare preset mode in `rango()` with environment-specific build setup
- `clientChunks` Vite plugin option (`false` | `true` | function; exported types
  `ClientChunks`, `ClientChunkMeta`) — per-route/per-feature splitting of the
  client (`"use client"`) bundle. The built-in strategy (`true`) groups app client
  modules by **route id** (the segment after a route-root marker such as
  `routes`/`app`/`pages`/`features`/`handlers`; an `app/` directly followed by
  another marker with a directory after it is a source root, so
  `app/routes/<id>/…` keys on `<id>` while `app/routes/Layout.tsx` stays
  `app-routes`, #1022),
  and returns `undefined` where
  there is no route structure so flat layouts and host-split sub-apps inherit the
  default grouping unchanged (no collision, no cross-app merge). A function is
  forwarded to `@vitejs/plugin-rsc`'s `clientChunks`. Shared runtime
  (React/router/`node_modules`) stays unsplit. **On by default pre-1.0**; opt out
  with `clientChunks: false`. See [client-chunking.md](../client-chunking.md).
  The built-in strategy is exported as `directoryClientChunks` so a custom
  function can OVERLAY it (route a few modules to a dedicated chunk, delegate
  the rest) instead of silently replacing route splitting for the whole app.
  A group is the loading unit (rendering any member downloads the whole group's
  chunk); `DEBUG=rango:chunks` logs each emitted group's client-reference count
  and size at build end (`clientChunksReport` in `vite/utils/client-chunks.ts`).
- Runtime CLI route extraction (`rango generate <paths>`) for CI and repo bootstrapping
- Debug surfaces: `debugManifest()`, `getMatchDebugStats()`, strict runtime/per-route tracing in development
- Internal instrumentation and plugin internals for multi-router deployments and manifest isolation
